title.zh: 卷八十二 列傳第七 十一宗諸子
title.en: Volume 82 Biographies 7: Sons of the Eleven Zongs
title.raw: 卷八十二 列傳第七 十一宗諸子 Volume 82 Biographies 7: Sons of the Eleven Zongs

sentences.zh: 十一宗諸子

translations.literal: Sons of the eleven zongs
translations.idiomatic: Sons of the Eleven Lineages

sentences.zh: 玄宗三十子：劉華妃生琮、第六子琬、第十二子璲，趙麗妃生瑛，元獻皇后生肅宗皇帝，錢妃生琰，皇甫德儀生瑤，劉才人生琚，武惠妃生一、第十五子敏、第十八子瑁、第二十一子琦，高婕妤生璬，郭順儀生璘，柳婕妤生玢，鐘美人生環，盧美人生瑝，閻才人生玼，王美人生珪，陳才人生珙，鄭才人生瑱，武賢儀生璿、第三十子璥；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had thirty sons: Consort Liu Huahua bore Cong, the sixth son Wan, and the twelfth son Sui; Consort Zhao Lihua bore Ying; Empress Yuanxian bore Emperor Suzong; Consort Qian bore Yan; Lady Huangfu Deyi bore Yao; Lady Liu the Talent bore Ju; Consort Wu Hui bore Yi, the fifteenth son Min, the eighteenth son Mao, and the twenty-first son Qi; Lady Gao the Jieyu bore Jiao; Lady Guo the Shunyi bore Lin; Lady Liu the Jieyu bore Bin; Lady Zhong the Beauty bore Huan; Lady Lu the Beauty bore Huang; Lady Yan the Talent bore Ci; Lady Wang the Beauty bore Gui; Lady Chen the Talent bore Gong; Lady Zheng the Talent bore Zhen; Lady Wu the Xianyi bore Xuan and the thirtieth son Jin;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had thirty sons. Consort Liu Huahua gave birth to Cong, the sixth son Wan, and the twelfth son Sui. Consort Zhao Lihua bore Ying. Empress Yuanxian bore Emperor Suzong. Consort Qian bore Yan. Lady Huangfu Deyi bore Yao. Lady Liu the Talent bore Ju. Consort Wu Hui bore Yi, the fifteenth son Min, the eighteenth son Mao, and the twenty-first son Qi. Lady Gao the Jieyu bore Jiao. Lady Guo the Shunyi bore Lin. Lady Liu the Jieyu bore Bin. Lady Zhong the Beauty bore Huan. Lady Lu the Beauty bore Huang. Lady Yan the Talent bore Ci. Lady Wang the Beauty bore Gui. Lady Chen the Talent bore Gong. Lady Zheng the Talent bore Zhen. Lady Wu the Xianyi bore Xuan and the thirtieth son Jin.

sentences.zh: 余七子夭，母氏失傳。

translations.literal: The remaining seven sons died young; their mothers' names are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Seven other sons died in infancy, and the identities of their mothers are unknown.

sentences.zh: 奉天皇帝琮，景雲元年，王許昌郡，與真定王同封。

translations.literal: Emperor Fengtian Cong—in the first year of Jingyun was made Prince of Xuchang commandery, enfeoffed together with the Prince of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Fengtian Cong was first enfeoffed as Prince of Xuchang commandery in the first year of the Jingyun era, on the same occasion as the Prince of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 先天元年，進王郯，與郢王同封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantian he was advanced to Prince of Tan, enfeoffed together with the Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xiantian era he was promoted to Prince of Tan, enfeoffed on the same day as the Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，領安西大都護、安撫河東關內隴右諸蕃大使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan he held the posts of Protector-General of Anxi and Commissioner for Pacification of the Various Tribes of Hedong, Guannei, and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan he was appointed Protector-General of Anxi and commissioner charged with pacifying the various tribes of Hedong, Guannei, and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 十三年，徙王慶，與忠、棣、榮、光、儀、潁、永、壽、延、盛、濟十一王同封。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Prince of Qing, enfeoffed together with the eleven princes Zhong, Di, Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Shou, Yan, Sheng, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was reassigned as Prince of Qing, enfeoffed together with the eleven princes Zhong, Di, Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Shou, Yan, Sheng, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 十五年，與十王並領節度，不出閤。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he and ten other princes all held circuit commands in name, without leaving the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he and ten other princes were all given nominal circuit commands while remaining within the palace.

sentences.zh: 琮以涼州都督兼河西諸軍節度大使。

translations.literal: Cong served as Military Governor of Liangzhou and concurrently as Grand Military Commissioner of the various armies of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Cong held the posts of military governor of Liangzhou and grand military commissioner of the Hexi armies.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，改節河東。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao his command was changed to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao his command was transferred to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 十載薨，贈太子，謚靖德。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died; he was posthumously made crown prince and given the posthumous title Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year and was posthumously honored as crown prince with the posthumous title Jingde.

sentences.zh: 肅宗立，詔曰：「靖德太子琮，親則朕兄，睿悊聰明，朕昔踐儲極，顧誠非次，君父有命，不敢違，永言懇讓，不克如素。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne, an edict said: 'Crown Prince Jingde Cong is in kinship my elder brother, wise and intelligent. When I formerly ascended the heir's position, I saw that it was truly out of order; my lord and father had a command, and I dared not disobey. I ever spoke earnest deferral, yet could not succeed as before.'
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, he issued an edict: 'Crown Prince Jingde Cong was my elder brother by kinship—wise and perceptive. When I first ascended the heir's position, I knew it was truly out of proper order, but my father and sovereign had commanded it and I dared not refuse. I pleaded earnestly to yield, yet could not restore things as they had been.'

sentences.zh: 宜進謚奉天皇帝，妃竇為恭應皇后。

translations.literal: He should be advanced in posthumous title to Emperor Fengtian, and his consort Dou made Empress Gongying.
translations.idiomatic: He should be posthumously elevated to Emperor Fengtian, and his consort Dou to Empress Gongying.

sentences.zh: 」詔尚書右仆射裴冕持節改葬，群臣素服臨送達禮門，帝禦門哭以過喪，墓號齊陵。

translations.literal: ' An edict ordered the Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Pei Mian to bear the staff and reinter the remains. The ministers in plain dress escorted the funeral to the Gate of Attaining Rites; the emperor stood at the gate and wept in mourning beyond the norm. The tomb was called Qiling.
translations.idiomatic: ' He ordered Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Pei Mian to bear the imperial staff and conduct a reburial. Ministers in plain dress escorted the funeral procession to the Gate of Attaining Rites, and the emperor stood at the gate and wept beyond the usual mourning rites. The tomb was named Qiling.

sentences.zh: 無子，以太子瑛子俅嗣王。

translations.literal: He had no sons; the crown prince Ying's son Qiu succeeded to the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons, so Crown Prince Ying's son Qiu succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 琮始名嗣直，太子嗣謙，棣王嗣真，鄂王嗣初，靖恭太子嗣玄。

translations.literal: Cong was originally named Sizhi; the crown prince Siqian; the Prince of Di Sizhen; the Prince of E Sichu; Crown Prince Jinggong Sixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was originally named Sizhi; the crown prince was Siqian; the Prince of Di, Sizhen; the Prince of E, Sichu; and Crown Prince Jinggong, Sixuan.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年，更名曰潭，曰鴻，曰洽，曰涓，曰滉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan their names were changed to Tan, Hong, Qia, Juan, and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan their names were changed to Tan, Hong, Qia, Juan, and Huang.

sentences.zh: 後十年改今名。

translations.literal: Ten years later they were given their present names.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later they received their present names.

sentences.zh: 太子瑛，始王真定，進王郢。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Ying was first made Prince of Zhending and then advanced to Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Ying was first enfeoffed as Prince of Zhending and later promoted to Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 開元三年，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyuan he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaiyuan he was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔太子、諸王入國學行齒胄禮，太常擇日謁孔子，太子獻。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict ordered the crown prince and the princes to enter the Directorate of Education to perform the cap-and-girdle rite; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices chose a day to visit Confucius, and the crown prince made the offering.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the crown prince and the princes were ordered into the Directorate of Education to perform the cap-and-girdle ceremony. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices chose a day to visit Confucius, and the crown prince presented the offering.

sentences.zh: 詔右散騎常侍褚無量執經，群臣、學官、諸生以差賜帛。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Right Regular Attendant Chu Wuliang to expound the classics; ministers, academy officials, and students were given silk according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Wuliang, Right Regular Attendant, was ordered to expound the classics, and ministers, academy officials, and students were rewarded with silk according to rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，瑛加元服，見太廟。

translations.literal: The next year Ying received the capping ceremony and visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Ying underwent the capping ceremony and visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 十六年，詔九品官息女可配太子者，有司采閱待進止，以太常少卿薛縚女為妃。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year an edict said that daughters of officials of the ninth rank and above who might be matched to the crown prince should be gathered and reviewed for imperial decision; the daughter of the Vice Minister of Rites Xue Zong was made consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year officials were ordered to gather and review eligible daughters of ninth-rank officials and above for possible marriage to the crown prince. The daughter of Vice Minister of Rites Xue Zong was chosen as his consort.

sentences.zh: 帝種麥苑中，瑛、諸王侍登，帝曰：「是將薦宗廟，故親之，亦欲若等知稼穡之難。

translations.literal: The emperor planted wheat in the palace park; Ying and the princes attended him as he went up, and the emperor said: 'This is to be offered to the ancestral temple, hence I tend it myself. I also wish you to know how hard farming is.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planted wheat in the palace park, with Ying and the princes in attendance. He said, 'This crop is destined for the ancestral temple, which is why I tend it myself. I also want you to understand how arduous farming truly is.'

sentences.zh: 」因分賜侍臣，曰：「《春秋》書『無麥禾』，古所甚重。

translations.literal: ' He then distributed portions to the attending ministers and said: 'The Spring and Autumn Annals records "no wheat or grain"—the ancients regarded this as gravely important.'
translations.idiomatic: ' He then distributed portions to the attending ministers and said, 'The Spring and Autumn Annals records "no wheat or grain"—the ancients regarded this as gravely important.'

sentences.zh: 比詔使者閱田畝，所對不以實，故朕自蒔以觀其成」雲。

translations.literal: Recently I ordered envoys to inspect the fields, but their reports were not truthful, so I plant myself to observe how the crop turns out,' he said.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I ordered envoys to inspect the fields, but their reports were not truthful, so I am planting the crop myself to see how it turns out,' he said.

sentences.zh: 初，瑛母以倡進，善歌舞，帝在潞得幸。

translations.literal: At first Ying's mother entered as a performer, skilled in song and dance; the emperor favored her while at Lu.
translations.idiomatic: At first Ying's mother had entered court as a performer skilled in song and dance, and the emperor favored her while he was still at Lu.

sentences.zh: 及即位，擢妃父元禮、兄常奴皆至大官。

translations.literal: When he took the throne he promoted the consort's father Yuan Li and her brother Changnu to high office.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne he promoted the consort's father Yuan Li and her brother Changnu to high office.

sentences.zh: 鄂、光二王母亦帝為臨淄王時以色選。

translations.literal: The mothers of the Princes of E and Guang were also chosen for their beauty when the emperor was Prince of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: The mothers of the Princes of E and Guang had likewise been chosen for their beauty when the emperor was still Prince of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 及武惠妃寵幸傾後宮，生壽王，愛與諸子絕等。

translations.literal: When Consort Wu Hui's favor dominated the inner palace and she bore the Prince of Shou, the emperor's love for him was unlike that for any other son.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Wu Hui's favor came to dominate the inner palace and she bore the Prince of Shou, the emperor's love for him was unlike that for any other son.

sentences.zh: 而太子、二王以母失職，頗怏怏。

translations.literal: But the crown prince and the two princes, because their mothers had lost standing, were rather discontented.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and the two princes, however, were deeply discontented because their mothers had fallen from favor.

sentences.zh: 惠妃女咸宜公主婿楊洄揣妃旨，伺太子短，嘩為醜語，惠妃訴於帝，且泣，帝大怒，召宰相議廢之。

translations.literal: Consort Hui's daughter, the Princess of Xianyi, had a son-in-law Yang Hui who divined the consort's intent, watched for the crown prince's faults, and spread ugly rumors. The consort complained to the emperor and wept; the emperor was greatly angered and summoned the chief ministers to discuss deposing him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hui, son-in-law of Consort Hui's daughter the Princess of Xianyi, divined the consort's wishes, watched for the crown prince's faults, and spread slanderous rumors. The consort complained to the emperor in tears; enraged, he summoned the chief ministers to discuss deposing the heir.

sentences.zh: 中書令張九齡諫曰：「太子、諸王日受聖訓，天下共慶。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling remonstrated: 'The crown prince and the princes daily receive your sacred instruction; all under Heaven rejoices together.'
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling remonstrated: 'The crown prince and the princes receive your sacred instruction every day, and all under Heaven rejoices in this.'

sentences.zh: 陛下享國久，子孫蕃衍，奈何一日棄三子。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has long enjoyed the realm and your descendants flourish—how can you in a single day cast aside three sons?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has long held the realm and your descendants flourish—how can you cast aside three sons in a single day?

sentences.zh: 昔晉獻公惑嬖姬之讒，申生憂死，國乃大亂；

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Xian of Jin was deluded by the favorite concubine's slander; Shen Sheng died in grief and the state fell into great disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Xian of Jin was deluded by his favorite concubine's slander; Shen Sheng died in grief and the state fell into chaos;

sentences.zh: 漢武帝信江充巫蠱，禍及太子，京師蹀血；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han believed Jiang Chong's witchcraft charges, calamity reached the crown prince, and the capital trampled blood;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han believed Jiang Chong's witchcraft charges, calamity reached the crown prince, and the capital ran with blood;

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝有賢子，賈後譖之，乃至喪亡；

translations.literal: Emperor Hui of Jin had a worthy son; Empress Jia slandered him, and ruin followed;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin had a worthy son, but Empress Jia slandered him and ruin followed;

sentences.zh: 隋文帝聽後言，廢太子勇，遂失天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui listened to the empress and deposed Crown Prince Yong, and thus lost the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui listened to the empress, deposed Crown Prince Yong, and thus lost the realm.

sentences.zh: 今太子無過，二王賢。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince has no fault, and the two princes are worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Today the crown prince is without fault, and the two princes are worthy men.

sentences.zh: 父子之道，天性也，雖有失，尚當掩之。

translations.literal: The way of father and son is nature's law; even if there are faults, they should still be covered.
translations.idiomatic: The bond between father and son is nature's law; even when there are faults, they should be covered over.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下裁赦。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty judge and pardon.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to judge and grant pardon.

sentences.zh: 」帝默然，太子得不廢。

translations.literal: ' The emperor was silent, and the crown prince was not deposed.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor fell silent, and the crown prince was not deposed.

sentences.zh: 俄而九齡罷，李林甫專國，數稱壽王美以揠妃意，妃果德之。

translations.literal: Soon Jiuling was dismissed; Li Linfu monopolized the state and repeatedly praised the Prince of Shou's excellence to please the consort, and the consort indeed was grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jiuling was dismissed. Li Linfu monopolized power and repeatedly praised the Prince of Shou to please the consort, who was duly grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，洄復構瑛、瑤、琚與妃之兄薛銹異謀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Hui again framed Ying, Yao, and Ju together with the consort's brother Xue Xiu in a treasonous plot.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Yang Hui again framed Ying, Yao, and Ju together with the consort's brother Xue Xiu in a treasonous plot.

sentences.zh: 惠妃使人詭召太子、二王，曰：「宮中有賊，請介以入。

translations.literal: Consort Hui sent someone to summon the crown prince and the two princes under false pretenses, saying: 'There are bandits in the palace—please enter armed.'
translations.idiomatic: Consort Hui sent someone to summon the crown prince and the two princes under false pretenses, saying, 'There are bandits in the palace—please enter armed.'

sentences.zh: 」太子從之。

translations.literal: ' The crown prince complied.
translations.idiomatic: ' The crown prince complied.

sentences.zh: 妃白帝曰：「太子、二王謀反，甲而來。

translations.literal: The consort told the emperor: 'The crown prince and the two princes are rebelling—they come in armor.'
translations.idiomatic: The consort told the emperor, 'The crown prince and the two princes are rebelling—they are coming in armor.'

sentences.zh: 」帝使中人視之，如言，遽召宰相林甫議，答曰：「陛下家事，非臣所宜豫。

translations.literal: ' The emperor sent eunuchs to look—it was as she said. He hastily summoned Chief Minister Linfu to discuss it. Linfu answered: 'This is Your Majesty's family affair; it is not for your servant to intrude.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor sent eunuchs to look, and it was as she said. He hastily summoned Chief Minister Linfu, who replied, 'This is Your Majesty's family affair—not something your servant should intrude upon.'

sentences.zh: 」帝意決，乃詔：「太子瑛、鄂王瑤、光王琚同惡均罪，並廢為庶人；

translations.literal: ' The emperor's mind was set, and he issued an edict: 'Crown Prince Ying, the Prince of E Yao, and the Prince of Guang Ju share equal guilt in the same evil and are all deposed to commoners;
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor's mind was made up, and he issued an edict: 'Crown Prince Ying, the Prince of E Yao, and the Prince of Guang Ju share equal guilt and are all deposed to commoner status;

sentences.zh: 銹賜死。

translations.literal: Xiu was granted death.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was ordered to take his own life.'

sentences.zh: 」瑛、瑤、琚尋遇害，天下冤之，號「三庶人」。

translations.literal: ' Ying, Yao, and Ju soon met violent deaths; all under Heaven regarded it as unjust and called them 'the three commoners.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Ying, Yao, and Ju were soon killed. All under Heaven regarded it as a grievous injustice and called them 'the Three Commoners.'

sentences.zh: 歲中，惠妃數見庶人為祟，因大病。

translations.literal: Within the year Consort Hui repeatedly saw the commoners as apparitions haunting her and fell gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year Consort Hui repeatedly saw the three men as haunting spirits and fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 夜召巫祈之，請改葬，且射行刑者瘞之，訖不解。

translations.literal: At night she summoned shamans to pray, requested reburial, and had the executioners shot and buried—yet she was not relieved.
translations.idiomatic: At night she summoned shamans to pray, requested that the victims be reburied, and had the executioners shot and buried—yet she found no relief.

sentences.zh: 妃死，崇亡。

translations.literal: When the consort died, the hauntings ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When the consort died, the hauntings ceased.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，詔贈瑛皇太子，瑤等復王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying an edict posthumously honored Ying as crown prince and restored Yao and the others as princes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying an edict posthumously honored Ying as crown prince and restored Yao and the others to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 瑛子五人：儼、伸、倩、俅、備。

translations.literal: Ying had five sons: Yan, Shen, Qian, Qiu, and Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had five sons: Yan, Shen, Qian, Qiu, and Bei.

sentences.zh: 瑛之廢，帝使慶王畜儼等為子。

translations.literal: When Ying was deposed, the emperor had the Prince of Qing raise Yan and the others as his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying was deposed, the emperor had the Prince of Qing adopt Yan and the others as his sons.

sentences.zh: 儼封新平郡王，伸平原郡王，俅嗣慶王，備太仆卿，倩失傳。

translations.literal: Yan was enfeoffed as Prince of Xinping commandery, Shen as Prince of Pingyuan commandery, Qiu succeeded as Prince of Qing, Bei became Minister of the Imperial Stud, and Qian's record is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was enfeoffed as Prince of Xinping commandery, Shen as Prince of Pingyuan commandery, Qiu succeeded to the title of Prince of Qing, Bei became Minister of the Imperial Stud, and Qian's record is lost.

sentences.zh: 隸王琰，開元二年始王鄫，與鄂、鄄二王同封。

translations.literal: Prince of Li Yan—in the second year of Kaiyuan was first made Prince of Zeng, enfeoffed together with the Princes of E and Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Li, Yan, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Zeng in the second year of Kaiyuan, on the same occasion as the Princes of E and Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 後徙王棣，領太原牧、太原以北諸軍節度大使。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Prince of Di and held the posts of Governor of Taiyuan and Grand Military Commissioner of the armies north of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reassigned as Prince of Di and appointed governor of Taiyuan and grand military commissioner of the armies north of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，為武威郡都督，經略節度河西、隴右。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was Military Governor of Wuwei commandery and commissioner overseeing and commanding Hexi and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he served as military governor of Wuwei commandery and commissioner overseeing Hexi and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 會妃韋以過置別室，而二孺人爭寵不平，求巫者密置符琰履中以求媚。

translations.literal: When Consort Wei was set aside in a separate chamber for a fault, two concubines quarreled over favor and sought a shaman to secretly place talismans in Yan's shoes to win his affection.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Wei was confined to a separate chamber for an offense, two junior consorts quarreled over favor and hired a shaman to secretly place talismans in Yan's shoes to win his affection.

sentences.zh: 仇人告琰厭魅上，帝伺其朝，使人取履視之，信。

translations.literal: An enemy reported that Yan had used sorcery against the emperor; the emperor waited until his audience, had someone take his shoes and look—he believed it.
translations.idiomatic: An enemy reported that Yan had used sorcery against the emperor. The emperor waited until his audience, had his shoes taken and examined, and believed the charge.

sentences.zh: 帝怒責琰，琰頓首謝曰：「臣罪宜死，然臣與婦不相見二年，有二孺人爭長，臣恐此三人為之。

translations.literal: The emperor angrily rebuked Yan; Yan kowtowed and said: 'Your servant deserves death, yet your servant and his wife have not seen each other for two years. Two concubines vie for precedence—I fear these three did it.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily rebuked Yan. Yan kowtowed and said, 'I deserve death, yet my wife and I have not seen each other for two years. Two junior consorts vie for precedence—I fear these three women are responsible.'

sentences.zh: 」及推，果驗。

translations.literal: ' When investigated, it proved true.
translations.idiomatic: ' When investigated, this proved true.

sentences.zh: 然帝猶疑琰，怒未置，太子以下皆為請，乃囚於鷹狗坊，以憂薨，妃，縚之女，無子，還本宗。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor still suspected Yan and his anger was not assuaged. From the crown prince down all pleaded for him, but he was imprisoned in the Hawk-and-Hound Ward and died of grief. His consort, daughter of Zong, had no sons and returned to her natal clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor still suspected Yan and his anger did not abate. From the crown prince downward all pleaded on his behalf, but he was imprisoned in the Hawk-and-Hound Ward and died of grief. His consort, daughter of Zong, had no sons and was returned to her natal clan.

sentences.zh: 琰凡五十五子，得王者四人，僎王汝南郡，僑宜都，俊濟南，侒順化；

translations.literal: Yan had fifty-five sons in all; four attained princely rank: Juan as Prince of Runan commandery, Qiao of Yidu, Jun of Jinan, and An of Shunhua;
translations.idiomatic: Yan had fifty-five sons in all. Four attained princely rank: Juan as Prince of Runan commandery, Qiao of Yidu, Jun of Jinan, and An of Shunhua;

sentences.zh: 僚太仆卿，俠國子祭酒，仁殿中監，僾秘書監。

translations.literal: Liao became Minister of the Imperial Stud, Xia Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, Ren Supervisor of the Palace, and Qian Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Liao became Minister of the Imperial Stud, Xia Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, Ren Supervisor of the Palace, and Qian Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，詔復琰王爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying an edict restored Yan's princely title.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying an edict restored Yan's princely title.

sentences.zh: 鄂王瑤，既封，遙領幽州都督、河北節度大使。

translations.literal: The Prince of E Yao, once enfeoffed, held in name the posts of Military Governor of Youzhou and Commissioner of the Hebei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of E, Yao, once enfeoffed, held in name the posts of military governor of Youzhou and commissioner of the Hebei circuit.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年，與榮、光、儀、潁、永、壽、延、盛、濟、信、義十一王並授開府儀同三司，實封二千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan he and the eleven princes Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Shou, Yan, Sheng, Ji, Xin, and Yi were all granted the rank of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with an actual fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan he and the eleven princes Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Shou, Yan, Sheng, Ji, Xin, and Yi were all granted the rank of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with an actual fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 詔詣東宮、尚書省，上日百官集送，有司供張設樂。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them to proceed to the Eastern Palace and the Department of State Affairs; on the day of presentation all officials gathered to escort them, and the relevant offices provided furnishings and set out music.
translations.idiomatic: They were ordered to proceed to the Eastern Palace and the Department of State Affairs. On the day of presentation all officials gathered to escort them, and the relevant offices provided furnishings and music.

sentences.zh: 是日，悉拜王府官屬，然未有府也，而選任冒濫，時不以為榮。

translations.literal: That day all were appointed to princely household offices, yet there were no actual households; appointments were recklessly excessive, and the age did not regard it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: That day all were appointed to princely household offices, yet there were no actual households to administer; appointments were recklessly excessive, and the age did not regard the honor as meaningful.

sentences.zh: 光王琚，開元十三年始王，與儀、潁、永、壽、延、盛、濟七王同封。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guang Ju—in the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan was first enfeoffed, together with the seven princes Yi, Ying, Yong, Shou, Yan, Sheng, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guang, Ju, was first enfeoffed in the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, together with the seven princes Yi, Ying, Yong, Shou, Yan, Sheng, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 俄領廣州都督。

translations.literal: Soon he held in name the post of Military Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he held in name the post of military governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 勇力善騎射，帝愛之。

translations.literal: Brave and strong, skilled in riding and archery—the emperor loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and strong, skilled in riding and archery, he was beloved by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 與鄂王同居，友睦甚，皆篤學。

translations.literal: He lived together with the Prince of E; their friendship was very close, and both were devoted to learning.
translations.idiomatic: He lived together with the Prince of E in close friendship, and both were devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 既廢，無嗣。

translations.literal: After his deposition he had no heirs.
translations.idiomatic: After his deposition he left no heirs.

sentences.zh: 初，琚名涺，儀王濰，潁王沄，永王澤，壽王清，延王洄，盛王沐，濟王溢，信王沔，義王漼，陳王沚，豐王澄，恒王潓，涼王漎，汴王滔，至二十三年，詔悉改今名。

translations.literal: At first Ju was named Ti; the Prince of Yi Wei; the Prince of Ying Yun; the Prince of Yong Ze; the Prince of Shou Qing; the Prince of Yan Hui; the Prince of Sheng Mu; the Prince of Ji Yi; the Prince of Xin Mian; the Prince of Yi Cui; the Prince of Chen Zhi; the Prince of Feng Cheng; the Prince of Heng Wo; the Prince of Liang Long; the Prince of Bian Tao—by the twenty-third year an edict ordered all to change to their present names.
translations.idiomatic: At first Ju was named Ti; the Prince of Yi, Wei; the Prince of Ying, Yun; the Prince of Yong, Ze; the Prince of Shou, Qing; the Prince of Yan, Hui; the Prince of Sheng, Mu; the Prince of Ji, Yi; the Prince of Xin, Mian; the Prince of Yi, Cui; the Prince of Chen, Zhi; the Prince of Feng, Cheng; the Prince of Heng, Wo; the Prince of Liang, Long; and the Prince of Bian, Tao. By the twenty-third year an edict ordered all to take their present names.

sentences.zh: 夏悼王一，生韶秀，以母寵，故鐘愛，命之曰一。

translations.literal: Prince Daohuai Yi was born graceful and fair; because of his mother's favor he was deeply cherished and named Yi ('One').
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daohuai Yi was born graceful and fair. Because of his mother's favor he was deeply cherished and given the name Yi ('One').

sentences.zh: 未免懷薨，追爵及謚。

translations.literal: Before leaving the womb he died; posthumous rank and title were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died before birth, and posthumous rank and title were granted.

sentences.zh: 時帝在東都，故葬龍門東岑，欲宮中望見雲。

translations.literal: The emperor was then in the Eastern Capital, so he was buried on the eastern slope of Longmen, that the palace might look out and see the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then in the Eastern Capital, so the child was buried on the eastern slope of Longmen so that the palace might look out and see the clouds above the grave.

sentences.zh: 儀王璲，即封，授河南牧。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi Sui was enfeoffed at once and appointed Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yi, Sui, was enfeoffed at once and appointed governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太傅。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 子侁王鐘陵郡，僆廣陵。

translations.literal: His son Shen was made Prince of Zhongling commandery, and Mian of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongling commandery, and Mian as Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 懷思王敏，貌豐秀若圖畫，帝愛之。

translations.literal: Prince Huaisi Min had a full, fair countenance as if painted; the emperor loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huaisi Min had a full, fair countenance as if painted on silk, and the emperor loved him.

sentences.zh: 甫晬薨，追爵及謚，祔葬敬陵。

translations.literal: He died just after his first birthday; posthumous rank and title were granted, and he was buried alongside Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: He died just after his first birthday. Posthumous rank and title were granted, and he was buried alongside Jingling.

sentences.zh: 永王璘，少失母，肅宗自養視之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yong Lin lost his mother young; Suzong himself raised and cared for him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yong, Lin, lost his mother while young, and Suzong himself raised and cared for him.

sentences.zh: 長聰敏好學。

translations.literal: When grown he was intelligent and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he proved intelligent and fond of learning.

sentences.zh: 貌陋甚，不能正視。

translations.literal: His appearance was very homely; he could not look people straight in the face.
translations.idiomatic: His appearance was very homely, and he could not look people straight in the face.

sentences.zh: 既封，領荊州大都督。

translations.literal: Once enfeoffed he held in name the post of Grand Protector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once enfeoffed he held in name the post of grand protector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，帝至扶風，詔璘即日赴鎮。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled the emperor reached Fufeng and ordered Lin to proceed to his post that very day.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled the emperor reached Fufeng and ordered Lin to proceed to his post that very day.

sentences.zh: 俄又領山南、江西、嶺南、黔中四道節度使，以少府監竇昭為副。

translations.literal: Soon he also held in name the four circuit commands of Shannan, Jiangxi, Lingnan, and Qianzhong, with the Director of the Palace Workshops Dou Zhao as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also held in name the four circuit commands of Shannan, Jiangxi, Lingnan, and Qianzhong, with Dou Zhao, Director of the Palace Workshops, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 璘至江陵，募士得數萬，補署郎官、御史。

translations.literal: Lin reached Jiangling, recruited troops numbering tens of thousands, and appointed supplemental court gentlemen and censors.
translations.idiomatic: Lin reached Jiangling, recruited tens of thousands of troops, and appointed supplemental court gentlemen and censors.

sentences.zh: 時江淮租賦巨億萬，在所山委。

translations.literal: At that time the land tax and tribute of the Jiang-Huai region amounted to hundreds of millions, piled mountain-high wherever stored.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the land tax and tribute of the Jiang-Huai region amounted to hundreds of millions, piled mountain-high wherever they were stored.

sentences.zh: 璘生宮中，於事不通曉，見富且強，遂有窺江左意，以薛镠、李臺卿、韋子春、劉巨鱗、蔡F駉為謀主。

translations.literal: Lin was born in the palace and understood nothing of affairs; seeing wealth and strength, he then harbored designs on the lands south of the Yangzi, taking Xue Liu, Li Taiqing, Wei Zichun, Liu Julin, and Cai Xide as his chief plotters.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had been born in the palace and understood nothing of practical affairs. Seeing the region's wealth and strength, he conceived designs on the lands south of the Yangzi and took Xue Liu, Li Taiqing, Wei Zichun, Liu Julin, and Cai Xide as his chief plotters.

sentences.zh: 肅宗聞之，詔璘還覲上皇於蜀，璘不從。

translations.literal: When Suzong heard of it he ordered Lin to return and attend the Retired Emperor in Shu; Lin did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong heard of it he ordered Lin to return and attend the Retired Emperor in Shu, but Lin refused.

sentences.zh: 其子襄城王亻易，剛鷙乏謀，亦樂亂，勸璘取金陵。

translations.literal: His son, the Prince of Xiangcheng Yi, was fierce and ruthless but lacking in strategy; he too delighted in disorder and urged Lin to seize Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: His son, the Prince of Xiangcheng Yi, was fierce and ruthless but lacking in strategy. He too delighted in disorder and urged Lin to seize Jinling.

sentences.zh: 即引舟師東下，甲士五千趨廣陵，以渾惟明、季廣琛、高仙琦為將，然未敢顯言取江左也。

translations.literal: He then led his fleet eastward; five thousand armored troops pressed toward Guangling, with Hun Weiming, Ji Guangchen, and Gao Xianqi as generals—yet he still did not dare openly speak of seizing the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his fleet eastward. Five thousand armored troops pressed toward Guangling under the generals Hun Weiming, Ji Guangchen, and Gao Xianqi—yet he still did not dare openly declare his intent to seize the lands south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 會吳郡采訪使李希言平牒璘，璘因發怒曰：「寡人上皇子，皇帝弟，地尊禮絕。

translations.literal: When the Jiangsu circuit investigating commissioner Li Xiyan sent Lin a dispatch on equal footing, Lin grew angry and said: 'I am the Retired Emperor's son and the emperor's younger brother—my station is exalted and my ritual standing supreme.'
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangsu circuit investigating commissioner Li Xiyan addressed Lin in a dispatch on equal terms, Lin flew into a rage and said, 'I am the Retired Emperor's son and the emperor's younger brother—my station is exalted and my ritual standing supreme.'

sentences.zh: 今希言乃平牒抗威，落筆署字，何邪？

translations.literal: Now Xiyan uses an equal dispatch to resist my authority and signs his name at the end—what is this?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xiyan uses an equal dispatch to defy my authority and signs his own name at the end—what does this mean?

sentences.zh: 」乃使惟明襲希言，而令廣琛趨廣陵，攻采訪使李成式。

translations.literal: ' He then sent Weiming to attack Xiyan and ordered Guangchen to hurry to Guangling to attack the investigating commissioner Li Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: ' He then sent Weiming to attack Xiyan and ordered Guangchen to hurry to Guangling to attack the investigating commissioner Li Chengshi.

sentences.zh: 璘至當塗，希言已屯丹楊，遣將元景曜等拒戰，不勝，降於璘，江淮震動。

translations.literal: Lin reached Dangtu; Xiyan had already encamped at Danyang and sent the generals Yuan Jingyao and others to resist— they were defeated and surrendered to Lin, and the Jiang-Huai region was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Lin reached Dangtu. Xiyan had already encamped at Danyang and sent Generals Yuan Jingyao and others to resist, but they were defeated and surrendered to Lin, throwing the Jiang-Huai region into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 明年，肅宗遣宦者啖廷瑤等與成式謀招喻之。

translations.literal: The next year Suzong sent the eunuch Dan Tingyao and others to join Chengshi in planning to win Lin over by persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Suzong sent the eunuch Dan Tingyao and others to join Chengshi in planning to win Lin over through persuasion.

sentences.zh: 時河北招討判官李銑在廣陵，有兵千余，廷瑤邀銑屯揚子，成式又遣裴戎以廣陵卒三千戍伊婁埭，張旗幟，大閱士。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xian, adjutant of the Hebei pacification campaign, was at Guangling with more than a thousand troops; Tingyao invited Xian to encamp at Yangzi. Chengshi also sent Pei Rong with three thousand Guangling soldiers to garrison Yilou dam, raising banners and holding a great review of troops.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Xian, adjutant of the Hebei pacification campaign, was at Guangling with more than a thousand troops. Tingyao invited Xian to encamp at Yangzi, while Chengshi sent Pei Rong with three thousand Guangling soldiers to garrison Yilou dam, raising banners and holding a grand troop review.

sentences.zh: 璘與亻易登陴望之，有懼色。

translations.literal: Lin and Yi climbed the battlements to look out and showed fear.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and Yi climbed the battlements to look out, and their faces showed fear.

sentences.zh: 廣琛知事不集，謂諸將曰：「與公等從王，豈欲反邪？

translations.literal: Guangchen knew the affair would not succeed and said to the generals: 'When you followed the prince with me, did you mean to rebel?'
translations.idiomatic: Guangchen knew the venture would not succeed and said to the generals, 'When you followed the prince with me, did you intend to rebel?'

sentences.zh: 上皇播遷，道路不通，而諸子無賢於王者。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor is in exile and the roads are blocked, yet among the sons none is worthier than the prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor is in exile and the roads are cut off, yet among the sons none is worthier than our prince.

sentences.zh: 如總江淮銳兵，長驅雍、洛，大功可成。

translations.literal: If we gather the elite troops of the Jiang-Huai and drive straight to Yong and Luo, great merit can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: If we gather the elite troops of the Jiang-Huai and drive straight to Yong and Luo, great merit can still be achieved.

sentences.zh: 今乃不然，使吾等名絓叛逆，如後世何？

translations.literal: Now it is not so, and you make our names entangled with rebellion—what shall we say to posterity?
translations.idiomatic: Now it is otherwise, and you bind our names to rebellion—what shall we say to posterity?

sentences.zh: 」眾許諾，遂割臂盟。

translations.literal: ' All assented and thereupon cut their arms to swear alliance.
translations.idiomatic: ' All assented, and they cut their arms to swear alliance.

sentences.zh: 於是惟明奔江寧，馮季康奔白沙，廣琛以兵六千奔廣陵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Weiming fled to Jiangning, Feng Jikang to Baisha, and Guangchen with six thousand troops fled to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Weiming fled to Jiangning, Feng Jikang to Baisha, and Guangchen fled to Guangling with six thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 璘使騎追躡之，廣琛曰：「我德王，故不忍決戰，逃命歸國耳。

translations.literal: Lin sent cavalry in pursuit; Guangchen said: 'I am grateful to the prince and therefore could not bear a decisive battle—I am only fleeing for my life to return to the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Lin sent cavalry in pursuit. Guangchen said, 'I am grateful to the prince and could not bear to fight him to the death—I am only fleeing for my life to return to the state.'

sentences.zh: 若逼我，且決死。

translations.literal: If you press me, I will fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: If you press me, I will fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 」追者止，乃免。

translations.literal: ' The pursuers halted, and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: ' The pursuers halted, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 是夜，銑陣江北，夜然束葦，人執二炬，景亂水中，覘者以倍告，璘軍亦舉火應之。

translations.literal: That night Xian arrayed his troops on the north bank of the river; at night they lit bundles of reeds, each man holding two torches, so that the scene in the water was confused. Scouts reported double the force, and Lin's army also raised fires in response.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xian arrayed his troops on the north bank. They lit bundles of reeds at night, each man holding two torches, so that the reflections in the water seemed to double their numbers. Scouts reported the enemy had crossed in force, and Lin's army also raised fires in response.

sentences.zh: 璘疑王師已濟，攜兒女及麾下遁去。

translations.literal: Lin suspected the imperial army had already crossed and fled with his children and followers.
translations.idiomatic: Lin suspected the imperial army had already crossed the river and fled with his children and followers.

sentences.zh: 遲明覺其紿，復入城，具舟楫，使亻易驅眾趨晉陵。

translations.literal: At dawn he realized he had been deceived, re-entered the city, prepared boats, and had Yi drive the troops toward Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he realized he had been deceived, returned to the city, prepared boats, and sent Yi to drive the troops toward Jinling.

sentences.zh: 諜者告曰：「王走矣！

translations.literal: A spy reported: 'The prince has fled!'
translations.idiomatic: A spy reported, 'The prince has fled!'

sentences.zh: 」成式以兵進，先鋒至新豐，璘使亻易、仙琦逆擊之。

translations.literal: ' Chengshi advanced with troops; the vanguard reached Xinfeng, and Lin sent Yi and Xianqi to strike them head-on.
translations.idiomatic: ' Chengshi advanced with troops. When the vanguard reached Xinfeng, Lin sent Yi and Xianqi to strike them head-on.

sentences.zh: 銑合勢，張左右翼，射亻易中肩，軍遂敗。

translations.literal: Xian combined forces, deployed both wings, shot Yi in the shoulder, and the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xian combined forces, deployed both wings, shot Yi in the shoulder, and the army was routed.

sentences.zh: 仙琦與璘奔鄱陽，司馬閉城拒，璘怒，焚城門入之，收庫兵，掠余幹，將南走嶺外。

translations.literal: Xianqi and Lin fled to Poyang; the prefect closed the city and refused them. Lin was enraged, burned the gate to enter, seized the arsenal weapons, plundered Yugan, and prepared to flee south beyond the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Xianqi and Lin fled to Poyang, but the prefect closed the city against them. Enraged, Lin burned the gate to enter, seized weapons from the arsenal, plundered Yugan, and prepared to flee south beyond the mountains.

sentences.zh: 皇甫侁兵追及之，戰大庾嶺，璘中矢被執，侁殺之。

translations.literal: Huangfu You's troops overtook them and fought at Dayu Ridge; Lin was struck by an arrow, captured, and You killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu You's troops overtook them and fought at Dayu Ridge. Lin was struck by an arrow, captured, and You killed him.

sentences.zh: 亻易為亂兵所害，仙琦逃去。

translations.literal: Yi was killed by mutinous soldiers; Xianqi escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was killed by mutinous soldiers, and Xianqi escaped.

sentences.zh: 璘未敗時，上皇下誥：「降為庶人，徙置房陵。

translations.literal: Before Lin's defeat the Retired Emperor issued an edict: 'Reduce him to commoner status and relocate him to Fangling.'
translations.idiomatic: Before Lin's defeat the Retired Emperor issued an edict: 'Reduce him to commoner status and relocate him to Fangling.'

sentences.zh: 」及死，侁送妻子至蜀，上皇傷悼久之。

translations.literal: ' When he died, You sent his wife and children to Shu; the Retired Emperor mourned for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: ' When he died, You sent his wife and children to Shu, and the Retired Emperor mourned for a long time.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以少所自鞠，不宣其罪。

translations.literal: Because Suzong had largely raised him himself, he did not proclaim his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Because Suzong had largely raised him himself, he did not publicly proclaim his crimes.

sentences.zh: 謂左右曰：「皇甫侁執吾弟，不送之蜀而擅殺之，何邪？

translations.literal: He said to those around him: 'Huangfu You seized my younger brother, did not send him to Shu, but killed him on his own authority—what is this?'
translations.idiomatic: He said to those around him, 'Huangfu You seized my younger brother, failed to send him to Shu, and killed him on his own authority—what does this mean?'

sentences.zh: 」由是不復用。

translations.literal: ' For this reason You was never again employed.
translations.idiomatic: ' For this reason You was never again employed.

sentences.zh: 薛寔等皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Xue Shi and the others were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shi and the others were all executed.

sentences.zh: 子儹為余姚王，偵莒國公，儇郕國公，伶、儀並國子祭酒。

translations.literal: His sons: Qian as Prince of Yuyao, Zhen as Duke of Ju, Xuan as Duke of Bin, and Ling and Yi both as Chancellors of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Qian, Prince of Yuyao; Zhen, Duke of Ju; Xuan, Duke of Bin; and Ling and Yi, both Chancellors of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 壽王瑁，母惠妃頻姙不育，及瑁生，寧王請養邸中，元妃自乳之，名為己子，故封比諸王最後。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shou Mao: his mother Consort Hui had been pregnant many times without bearing; when Mao was born, the Prince of Ning asked to raise him in his residence, and the primary consort nursed him herself and named him as her own son, hence his enfeoffment came last among the princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shou, Mao: his mother Consort Hui had been pregnant many times without bearing a child. When Mao was born, the Prince of Ning asked to raise him in his residence, and the primary consort nursed him herself and claimed him as her own son; hence his enfeoffment came last among the princes.

sentences.zh: 開元十五年，遙領益州大都督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaiyuan he held in name the post of Grand Protector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Kaiyuan he held in name the post of grand protector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以永王等尚幼，詔不入謁。

translations.literal: At first, because the Prince of Yong and others were still young, an edict ordered them not to attend audience.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because the Prince of Yong and others were still young, an edict ordered them not to attend imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 瑁七歲，請與諸兄眾謝，拜舞有儀矩，帝異之。

translations.literal: At seven Mao asked to join his elder brothers in mass thanksgiving; his bowing and dancing had proper form, and the emperor was struck by it.
translations.idiomatic: At seven Mao asked to join his elder brothers in mass thanksgiving. His bowing and dancing were properly formed, and the emperor was impressed.

sentences.zh: 寧王薨，請制服以報私恩，詔可。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ning died, Mao asked to wear mourning garb to repay a private debt of gratitude; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ning died, Mao asked to wear mourning garb to repay a private debt of gratitude, and an edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年薨，贈太傅。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth year of Dali and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Dali and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 子王者三人，僾王德陽郡，伓濟陽郡，偡廣陽郡，伉薛國公，傑國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Three sons attained princely rank: Qian as Prince of Deyang commandery, Fu of Jiyang commandery, Ting of Guangyang commandery; Kang as Duke of Xue; Jie as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Three sons attained princely rank: Qian as Prince of Deyang commandery, Fu of Jiyang, and Ting of Guangyang; Kang as Duke of Xue; and Jie as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 盛宣王琦，既封，領揚州大都督。

translations.literal: Prince Xuancheng of Sheng Qi, once enfeoffed, held in name the post of Grand Protector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xuancheng of Sheng, Qi, once enfeoffed, held in name the post of grand protector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝之西，詔為廣陵大都督、淮南江東河南節度大使，以劉匯為副，李成式為副大使，琦不行。

translations.literal: When the emperor went west, an edict made Qi Grand Protector of Guangling and Commissioner of the Huainan, Jiangdong, and Henan circuits, with Liu Hui as deputy and Li Chengshi as deputy commissioner; Qi did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went west, an edict appointed Qi grand protector of Guangling and commissioner of the Huainan, Jiangdong, and Henan circuits, with Liu Hui as deputy and Li Chengshi as deputy commissioner, but Qi did not go.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年薨，贈太傅。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Guangde and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Guangde and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 子償封真定王，佩武都王，俗徐國公，系許國公。

translations.literal: His sons: Chang enfeoffed as Prince of Zhending, Pei as Prince of Wudu, Su as Duke of Xu, and Xi as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Chang, enfeoffed as Prince of Zhending; Pei as Prince of Wudu; Su as Duke of Xu; and Xi as Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 濟王環，逸其薨年。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ji Huan—the year of his death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ji, Huan—the year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 子傃王永嘉郡，俛平樂郡。

translations.literal: His sons: Su as Prince of Yongjia commandery and Mian of Pingle commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Su, Prince of Yongjia commandery, and Mian, Prince of Pingle commandery.

sentences.zh: 信王瑝，開元二十一年始王，與義、陳、豐、恒、涼、汴六王同封。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xin Huang—in the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan was first enfeoffed, together with the six princes Yi, Chen, Feng, Heng, Liang, and Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xin, Huang, was first enfeoffed in the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan, together with the six princes Yi, Chen, Feng, Heng, Liang, and Bian.

sentences.zh: 子佟封新安王，倜晉陵王。

translations.literal: His son Tong was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an and Ti as Prince of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tong was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an and Ti as Prince of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 義王玼，與信王並失薨年。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi Ci—like the Prince of Xin, the year of death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yi, Ci—like the Prince of Xin, the year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 子儀為舞陽王，僇高密王。

translations.literal: His sons: Yi as Prince of Wuyang and Lu as Prince of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yi, Prince of Wuyang, and Lu, Prince of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 陳王珪，二十一子，得王者三人，倫王安南郡，佗臨淮，佼安陽。

translations.literal: The Prince of Chen Gui had twenty-one sons; three attained princely rank: Lun as Prince of Annan commandery, Tuo of Linhuai, and Jiao of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Chen, Gui, had twenty-one sons. Three attained princely rank: Lun as Prince of Annan commandery, Tuo of Linhuai, and Jiao of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 豐王珙，已封，為左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Feng Gong, already enfeoffed, became General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Feng, Gong, already enfeoffed, became General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝至普安，授珙武威都督、河西隴右安西北庭節度大使，以隴西太守鄧景山為副，珙不行。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Pu'an, Gong was appointed Military Governor of Wuwei and Commissioner of the Hexi, Longyou, Anxi, and Beiting circuits, with Deng Jingshan, Prefect of Longxi, as deputy; Gong did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Pu'an, Gong was appointed military governor of Wuwei and commissioner of the Hexi, Longyou, Anxi, and Beiting circuits, with Deng Jingshan, prefect of Longxi, as deputy, but Gong did not go.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，吐蕃入京師，代宗幸陜，將軍王懷忠閉苑門，以五百騎劫諸王西迎虜，遇郭子儀，懷忠曰：「上東遷，宗社無主，今仆奉諸王西奔，以系天下望。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangde the Tibetans entered the capital; Emperor Daizong fled to Shan. General Wang Huaizhong closed the park gates and with five hundred cavalry seized the princes to flee west and welcome the invaders. He met Guo Ziyi and said: 'The sovereign has moved east; the altars of state are without a master. Now your servant leads the princes west to sustain the hopes of the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guangde the Tibetans entered the capital and Emperor Daizong fled to Shan. General Wang Huaizhong closed the park gates and with five hundred cavalry seized the princes to flee west and welcome the invaders. He met Guo Ziyi and said, 'The sovereign has moved east and the altars of state are without a master. I am leading the princes west to sustain the hopes of the realm.'

sentences.zh: 公為元帥，惟所廢置。

translations.literal: You are the commander-in-chief—dispose as you will.'
translations.idiomatic: You are the commander-in-chief—dispose of us as you will.'

sentences.zh: 」子儀未對。

translations.literal: ' Ziyi did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: ' Ziyi did not answer.

sentences.zh: 珙輒曰：「公何如？

translations.literal: Gong then said: 'What do you think, sir?'
translations.idiomatic: Gong then said, 'What do you think, sir?'

sentences.zh: 」司馬王延昌質責珙曰：「上雖蒙塵，未有失德，王為籓翰，安得狂悖之言？

translations.literal: ' The prefectural marshal Wang Yanchang sternly rebuked Gong: 'Though the sovereign suffers exile, he has committed no fault. As a prince you are a bulwark of the realm—how can you utter such reckless words?'
translations.idiomatic: ' The prefectural marshal Wang Yanchang sternly rebuked Gong: 'Though the sovereign suffers exile, he has committed no fault. As a prince you are a bulwark of the realm—how can you utter such reckless words?'

sentences.zh: 」子儀亦讓之，即護送行在所，帝赦不責。

translations.literal: ' Ziyi also reproved him, then escorted them to the emperor's temporary residence; the emperor pardoned and did not punish.
translations.idiomatic: ' Ziyi also reproved him, then escorted them to the emperor's temporary residence. The emperor pardoned them and did not punish.

sentences.zh: 珙語不遜，群臣恐其亂，請除之，乃賜死。

translations.literal: Gong's speech was insubordinate; the ministers feared he would cause disorder and asked that he be removed—he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's speech was insubordinate. The ministers feared he would cause disorder and asked that he be removed, and he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 子佻為齊安王。

translations.literal: His son Tiao was made Prince of Qi'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tiao was made Prince of Qi'an.

sentences.zh: 恒王瑱，好方士，常服道士服。

translations.literal: The Prince of Heng Zhen loved masters of the esoteric arts and often wore Daoist robes.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Heng, Zhen, loved masters of the esoteric arts and often wore Daoist robes.

sentences.zh: 從帝幸蜀，還，代宗時薨。

translations.literal: He accompanied the emperor to Shu and returned; he died in the time of Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Shu and returned, and died during the reign of Daizong.

sentences.zh: 涼王璿，母高平王重規之女，宮中號小武妃者。

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang Xuan: his mother was the daughter of the Prince of Gaoping Chonggui, known in the palace as the Lesser Lady Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang, Xuan: his mother was the daughter of the Prince of Gaoping Chonggui, known in the palace as the Lesser Lady Wu.

sentences.zh: 璿薨代宗時。

translations.literal: Xuan died in the time of Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan died during the reign of Daizong.

sentences.zh: 子仂為瀘陽郡王。

translations.literal: His son Le was made Prince of Luyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Le was made Prince of Luyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 唐制：親王封戶八百，增至千；

translations.literal: Tang institution: imperial princes received eight hundred fief households, increased to one thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang institutions, imperial princes received eight hundred fief households, later increased to one thousand;

sentences.zh: 公主三百，長公主止六百。

translations.literal: princesses three hundred, grand princesses no more than six hundred.
translations.idiomatic: princesses three hundred, and grand princesses no more than six hundred.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，沛英豫三王、太平公主武後所生，戶始逾制，垂拱中，太平至千二百戶。

translations.literal: Under Gaozong the three princes Pei, Ying, and Yu and the Princess Taiping, born of Empress Wu, first exceeded the regulation; in the Chuigong era Taiping reached twelve hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong the three princes Pei, Ying, and Yu and the Princess Taiping, born of Empress Wu, first exceeded the regulation. In the Chuigong era Taiping reached twelve hundred households.

sentences.zh: 聖歷初，相王、太平皆三千，壽春等五王各三百。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengli the Prince of Xiang and Taiping each had three thousand; the five princes including Shouchun each had three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shengli era the Prince of Xiang and Taiping each had three thousand households, while the five princes including Shouchun each had three hundred.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，相王、太平至五千，衛王三千，溫王二千，壽春等王皆七百，嗣雍、衡陽、臨淄、巴陵、中山王五百，安樂公主二千，長寧千五百，宣城、宜城、宣安各千，相王女為縣主，各三百。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong the Prince of Xiang and Taiping reached five thousand; the Prince of Wei three thousand; the Prince of Wen two thousand; the princes including Shouchun all seven hundred; the heirs of Yong, Hengyang, Linzi, Baling, and Zhongshan five hundred each; the Princess Anle two thousand; Changning fifteen hundred; Xuancheng, Yicheng, and Xuan'an each one thousand; the Prince of Xiang's daughters as county mistresses each three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shenlong the Prince of Xiang and Taiping reached five thousand households; the Prince of Wei three thousand; the Prince of Wen two thousand; the princes including Shouchun seven hundred each; the heirs of Yong, Hengyang, Linzi, Baling, and Zhongshan five hundred each; the Princess Anle two thousand; Changning fifteen hundred; Xuancheng, Yicheng, and Xuan'an one thousand each; and the Prince of Xiang's daughters as county mistresses three hundred each.

sentences.zh: 相王增至七千，安樂三千，長寧二千五百，宜城以下二千。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiang was increased to seven thousand; Anle to three thousand; Changning to twenty-five hundred; Yicheng and below to two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiang was increased to seven thousand; Anle to three thousand; Changning to twenty-five hundred; and Yicheng and below to two thousand.

sentences.zh: 相王、太平、長寧、安樂以七丁為限，雖水旱不蠲，以國租、庸滿之。

translations.literal: For the Prince of Xiang, Taiping, Changning, and Anle the limit was seven adult males; even in flood or drought there was no exemption—they were made up from state land tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: For the Prince of Xiang, Taiping, Changning, and Anle the limit was seven adult males per household. Even in flood or drought there was no exemption—the shortfall was made up from state land tax and corvée revenue.

sentences.zh: 中宗遺詔，雍、壽春王進為親王，戶千。

translations.literal: In Zhongzong's testamentary edict the Princes of Yong and Shouchun were advanced to full imperial princes with one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongzong's testamentary edict the Princes of Yong and Shouchun were advanced to full imperial princes with one thousand households each.

sentences.zh: 開元後，天子敦睦兄弟，故寧王戶至五千五百，岐、薛五千，申王以外家微，戶四千，邠王千八百，帝妹戶千，中宗諸女如之，通以三丁為限。

translations.literal: After Kaiyuan the Son of Heaven cultivated brotherly harmony, so the Prince of Ning reached fifty-five hundred households, Qi and Xue five thousand, the Prince of Shen four thousand because his mother's family was slight, the Prince of Bin eighteen hundred, the emperor's sisters one thousand, Zhongzong's daughters likewise—the general limit was three adult males.
translations.idiomatic: After Kaiyuan the emperor cultivated brotherly harmony, so the Prince of Ning reached fifty-five hundred households, Qi and Xue five thousand, the Prince of Shen four thousand because his mother's family was of low standing, the Prince of Bin eighteen hundred, and the emperor's sisters one thousand, with Zhongzong's daughters treated likewise—the general limit being three adult males.

sentences.zh: 及皇子封王，戶二千，公主五百。

translations.literal: When imperial sons were enfeoffed as princes they received two thousand households; princesses five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial sons were enfeoffed as princes they received two thousand households, and princesses five hundred.

sentences.zh: 咸宜公主以母惠妃故，封至千，自是，諸公主例千戶止。

translations.literal: The Princess of Xianyi, because her mother was Consort Hui, received a fief of one thousand; from then on princesses were generally limited to one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Xianyi, because her mother was Consort Hui, received a fief of one thousand households. From then on princesses were generally limited to one thousand.

sentences.zh: 初，文德皇后崩，晉王最幼，太宗憐之，不使出閤。

translations.literal: At first, when Empress Wende died, the Prince of Jin was youngest; Taizong pitied him and did not let him leave the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Empress Wende died, the Prince of Jin was the youngest child. Taizong pitied him and would not let him leave the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 豫王亦以武後少子不出閤，嗣聖初，即帝位，及降封相王，乃出閤。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yu likewise, as Empress Wu's youngest son, did not leave the inner quarters; at the beginning of Sisheng he took the throne, and only when demoted to Prince of Xiang did he leave the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yu likewise, as Empress Wu's youngest son, did not leave the inner quarters. At the beginning of Sisheng he took the throne, and only when demoted to Prince of Xiang did he leave the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，譙王失愛，遷外籓，溫王年十七，猶居宮中，遂立為帝。

translations.literal: Under Zhongzong the Prince of Qiao lost favor and was moved to an outer fief; the Prince of Wen at seventeen still lived in the palace and was thereupon established as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongzong the Prince of Qiao lost favor and was moved to an outer fief. The Prince of Wen, at seventeen, still lived in the palace and was thereupon established as emperor.

sentences.zh: 開元後，皇子幼，多居禁內，既長，詔附苑城為大宮，分院而處，號「十王宅」，所謂慶、忠、棣、鄂、榮、光、儀、潁、永、延、盛、濟等王，以十，舉全數也。

translations.literal: After Kaiyuan, while princes were young they mostly lived within the forbidden precincts; when grown, an edict ordered them lodged beside the park city in a great palace, dwelling in separate courtyards, called the 'Ten Princes' Residence'—the so-called Princes of Qing, Zhong, Di, E, Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Yan, Sheng, and Ji; 'ten' is used to mean the full number.
translations.idiomatic: After Kaiyuan, while princes were young they mostly lived within the forbidden precincts. When they grew up, an edict ordered them lodged beside the park city in a great palace, dwelling in separate courtyards called the 'Ten Princes' Residence'—the Princes of Qing, Zhong, Di, E, Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Yan, Sheng, and Ji. The term 'ten' is used to mean the full number.

sentences.zh: 中人押之，就夾城參天子起居。

translations.literal: Eunuchs escorted them through the walled passage to attend upon the Son of Heaven's daily movements.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs escorted them through the walled passage to attend upon the emperor's daily movements.

sentences.zh: 家令日進膳。

translations.literal: The household steward daily presented meals.
translations.idiomatic: The household steward presented meals daily.

sentences.zh: 引詞學士入授書，謂之侍讀。

translations.literal: Literary academicians were brought in to teach the classics, called attendants for study.
translations.idiomatic: Literary academicians were brought in to teach the classics; they were called attendants for study.

sentences.zh: 壽、信、義、陳、豐、恒、涼七王就封，亦居十宅。

translations.literal: The seven princes Shou, Xin, Yi, Chen, Feng, Heng, and Liang, though they went to their fiefs, also dwelt in the Ten Princes' Residence.
translations.idiomatic: The seven princes Shou, Xin, Yi, Chen, Feng, Heng, and Liang, though they went to their fiefs, also dwelt in the Ten Princes' Residence.

sentences.zh: 鄂、光廢死，忠王立為太子，慶、棣繼薨，唯榮、儀十四王居院，而府幕列於外坊，歲時通名起居。

translations.literal: E and Guang were deposed and died; the Prince of Zhong was established as crown prince; Qing and Di died in succession; only Rong, Yi, and fourteen princes dwelt in the compound, while household staffs were stationed in outer wards and at year's end sent their names to inquire after the emperor's well-being.
translations.idiomatic: E and Guang were deposed and died. The Prince of Zhong was established as crown prince, and Qing and Di died in succession. Only Rong, Yi, and fourteen other princes dwelt in the compound, while household staffs were stationed in outer wards and at year's end sent their names to inquire after the emperor's well-being.

sentences.zh: 既又諸孫多，則於宅外更置「百孫院」。

translations.literal: When there were many grandsons, outside the residence they further established the 'Hundred Grandsons' Court.'
translations.idiomatic: When there were many grandsons, they further established the 'Hundred Grandsons' Court' outside the residence.

sentences.zh: 天子歲幸華清宮，又置十王、百孫院於宮側。

translations.literal: Each year when the Son of Heaven visited Huaqing Palace, the Ten Princes' and Hundred Grandsons' courts were also set up beside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Each year when the emperor visited Huaqing Palace, the Ten Princes' and Hundred Grandsons' courts were also set up beside the palace.

sentences.zh: 宮人每院四百余，百孫院亦三四十人。

translations.literal: Palace women in each courtyard numbered more than four hundred; the Hundred Grandsons' Court also thirty or forty.
translations.idiomatic: Each courtyard had more than four hundred palace women, and the Hundred Grandsons' Court thirty or forty as well.

sentences.zh: 禁中置維城庫，以給諸王月奉。

translations.literal: Within the forbidden precincts a Weicheng Treasury was established to supply the princes' monthly stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Within the forbidden precincts a Weicheng Treasury was established to supply the princes' monthly stipends.

sentences.zh: 諸孫納妃、嫁女，就十王宅。

translations.literal: When grandsons took consorts or married daughters, it was done at the Ten Princes' Residence.
translations.idiomatic: When grandsons took consorts or married daughters, the ceremonies were held at the Ten Princes' Residence.

sentences.zh: 太子不居東宮，處乘輿所幸別院。

translations.literal: The crown prince did not dwell in the Eastern Palace but in a separate courtyard favored by the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince did not dwell in the Eastern Palace but in a separate courtyard favored by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 太子、親王、公主婚嫁並供帳於崇仁之禮院。

translations.literal: The crown prince's, imperial princes', and princesses' marriages all had provisions supplied at the Ritual Court of Chongren.
translations.idiomatic: Marriages of the crown prince, imperial princes, and princesses all had provisions supplied at the Ritual Court of Chongren.

sentences.zh: 此承平制雲。

translations.literal: These were institutions of peaceful times.
translations.idiomatic: These were institutions of peaceful times.

sentences.zh: 肅宗十四子：章敬皇后生代宗皇帝，宮人孫生系，張生倓，王生佖，陳婕妤生僅，韋妃生 ，張美人生侹，後宮生榮，裴昭儀生僙，段婕妤生倕，崔妃生偲，張皇后生佋，侗，後宮生僖。

translations.literal: Suzong had fourteen sons: Empress Zhangjing bore Emperor Daizong; the palace woman Sun bore Xi; Zhang bore Tan; Wang bore Bi; Lady Chen the Jieyu bore Jin; Consort Wei bore Shen; Lady Zhang the Beauty bore Ting; the rear palace bore Rong; Lady Pei the Zhaoyi bore Qian; Lady Duan the Jieyu bore Chun; Consort Cui bore Si; Empress Zhang bore Zhao and Tong; the rear palace bore Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong had fourteen sons. Empress Zhangjing bore Emperor Daizong. The palace woman Sun bore Xi; Zhang bore Tan; Wang bore Bi. Lady Chen the Jieyu bore Jin. Consort Wei bore Shen. Lady Zhang the Beauty bore Ting. The rear palace bore Rong. Lady Pei the Zhaoyi bore Qian. Lady Duan the Jieyu bore Chun. Consort Cui bore Si. Empress Zhang bore Zhao and Tong. The rear palace bore Xi.

sentences.zh: 越王系，生開元時。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yue Xi was born in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yue, Xi, was born in the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 玄宗末年，悉王太子子，故系王南陽郡。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanzong's reign all were made sons of the crown prince, hence Xi was made Prince of Nanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xuanzong's reign all were registered as sons of the crown prince, hence Xi was made Prince of Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，至德二載十二月，進王趙，與彭、兗、涇、鄆、襄、杞、召、興、定九王同封。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, in the twelfth month of the second year of Zhide Xi was advanced to Prince of Zhao, enfeoffed together with the nine princes Peng, Yan, Jing, Yun, Xiang, Qi, Shao, Xing, and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, in the twelfth month of the second year of Zhide Xi was advanced to Prince of Zhao, enfeoffed together with the nine princes Peng, Yan, Jing, Yun, Xiang, Qi, Shao, Xing, and Ding.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，九節度兵潰河北，朝廷震駭，乃以李光弼代郭子儀總兵關東，而光弼請賢王為帥，於是詔系充天下兵馬元帥，而光弼以司空兼侍中、薊國公副，知節度行營事，系留京師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan the troops of nine circuits collapsed in Hebei and the court was shaken. Li Guangbi was made to replace Guo Ziyi in commanding the armies east of the Pass; Guangbi requested a worthy prince as commander, and an edict appointed Xi as commander-in-chief of all armies under Heaven, with Guangbi as Vice Minister of Works and Palace Attendant, Duke of Ji, as deputy knowing the affairs of the circuit campaign headquarters—Xi remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianyuan the troops of nine circuits collapsed in Hebei and the court was shaken. Li Guangbi replaced Guo Ziyi in commanding the armies east of the Pass and requested a worthy prince as commander. An edict appointed Xi commander-in-chief of all armies under Heaven, with Guangbi, Vice Minister of Works and Palace Attendant and Duke of Ji, as deputy in charge of the circuit campaign headquarters—while Xi remained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 史思明陷洛陽，系請行，不聽。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming took Luoyang, Xi requested to go but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming took Luoyang, Xi requested to go but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙王越。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was reassigned as Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 帝寢疾，皇太子監國，張皇后與中人李輔國有隙，因召太子入，謂曰：「輔國典禁軍，用事久，四方詔令皆出其口，矯天子制，逼徙聖皇，天下側目。

translations.literal: The emperor lay ill in bed. The crown prince supervised the state. Empress Zhang had a rift with the eunuch Li Fuguo. She therefore summoned the crown prince in and said: "Fuguo commands the Forbidden Army and has held power long. Edicts from all four quarters issue from his mouth. He counterfeits the Son of Heaven's orders and forced the relocation of the Sacred Sovereign. All under Heaven look on askance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell gravely ill, the crown prince took charge of state affairs. Empress Zhang was at odds with the eunuch Li Fuguo. She summoned the crown prince and said, "Fuguo commands the Forbidden Army and has wielded power for years. Edicts from every quarter come from his mouth alone. He forges the Son of Heaven's orders and drove the retired emperor from the capital. The whole realm watches in alarm.

sentences.zh: 今上疾彌留，輔國常怏怏，忌吾與汝。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign's illness lingers near death. Fuguo is often discontent and envies me and you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's illness is now beyond hope. Fuguo has grown restless and bears ill will toward us both.

sentences.zh: 又程元振陰結黃門，圖不軌。

translations.literal: Moreover Cheng Yuanzhen secretly allies with the Yellow Gates and plots rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanzhen, moreover, has been secretly colluding with the palace eunuchs to plot treason.

sentences.zh: 若釋不誅，禍不移頃。

translations.literal: If you release them without execution, disaster will arrive in no time.
translations.idiomatic: If you spare them and do not put them to death, catastrophe will strike within moments.

sentences.zh: 」太子泣曰：「此二人者，陛下勛舊，而上體不豫，重以此事，得無震驚乎？

translations.literal: The crown prince wept and said: "These two men are Your Majesty's meritorious old servants, and the sovereign's person is unwell. To burden him further with this matter—would it not shock him terribly?
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wept and said, "These two are your majesty's old servants with meritorious service, and the emperor himself is unwell. To burden him with this on top of everything—would it not terrify him?

sentences.zh: 願出外徐計之。

translations.literal: I wish to go out and plan this at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Let me withdraw and consider the matter at leisure.

sentences.zh: 」後曰：「是難與共事者！

translations.literal: The empress said: "This is one hard to work with!
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "This is a man impossible to work with!

sentences.zh: 」乃召系曰：「汝能行此乎？

translations.literal: She then summoned Xi and said: "Can you carry this out?
translations.idiomatic: She then summoned Xi and asked, "Can you do this?

sentences.zh: 」系許諾。

translations.literal: Xi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xi agreed.

sentences.zh: 即遣內謁者監段恒俊選材勇宦者二百人，授甲長生殿，以帝命召太子。

translations.literal: At once she dispatched the Inner Usher Supervisor Duan Hengjun to select two hundred brave eunuchs, armed them in Changsheng Hall, and with the emperor's command summoned the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: She immediately sent the Inner Usher Supervisor Duan Hengjun to select two hundred stalwart eunuchs, issued them armor in Changsheng Hall, and summoned the crown prince in the emperor's name.

sentences.zh: 元振以告輔國，乃相與勒兵淩霄門，迎太子，以難告。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen reported to Fuguo. They then together led troops to Lingxiao Gate, welcomed the crown prince, and told him of the danger.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen informed Fuguo. The two then mustered troops at Lingxiao Gate, received the crown prince, and warned him of the plot.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「上疾亟，吾可懼死不赴乎？

translations.literal: The crown prince said: "The sovereign's illness is acute. How could I, fearing death, refuse to go?
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "The emperor is desperately ill. How could I, for fear of death, refuse to go to him?

sentences.zh: 」元振曰：「赴則及禍。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen said: "If you go you will meet disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen said, "If you go, you will walk into disaster.

sentences.zh: 」乃以兵護太子止飛龍廄，勒兵夜入三殿，收系及恒俊等百余人系之，幽後別殿。

translations.literal: They then used troops to protect the crown prince and detained him at Feilong Stable. They led troops by night into the Three Halls, seized Xi and Hengjun and more than a hundred others and bound them, and confined the empress in a separate hall.
translations.idiomatic: They then used armed guards to hold the crown prince at Feilong Stable. By night they led troops into the Three Halls, seized Xi, Hengjun, and more than a hundred others and bound them, and confined the empress in a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 後及系皆為輔國所害。

translations.literal: The empress and Xi were both killed by Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: Both the empress and Xi were killed by Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 系三子：建王武威郡，逌興道，逾齊國公。

translations.literal: Xi had three sons: the Prince of Jian held Wuwei commandery, You held Xingdao, and Yu was Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had three sons: the Prince of Jian, enfeoffed in Wuwei commandery; You, Grand Preceptor of Xingdao; and Yu, Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 承天皇帝倓，始王建寧。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengtian Tan, initially enfeoffed Prince of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengtian, Tan, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 英毅有才略。

translations.literal: Stern and resolute, with talent and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and resolute, with talent and strategic ability.

sentences.zh: 善騎射。

translations.literal: Skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 祿山亂，典親兵，扈車駕。

translations.literal: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, he commanded the intimate guard and escorted the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion erupted, he commanded the emperor's personal guard and escorted the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 度渭，百姓遮道留太子，太子使喻曰：「至尊播遷，吾可以違左右乎？

translations.literal: Crossing the Wei, the common people blocked the road to detain the crown prince. The crown prince sent someone to explain: "The Supreme Sovereign wanders in exile—how can I leave his side?
translations.idiomatic: At the Wei River the people blocked the road, begging the crown prince to stay. The crown prince sent word: "The emperor wanders in exile—how can I abandon his side?

sentences.zh: 」倓進說曰：「逆胡亂常，四海崩分，不因人情圖興復，雖欲從上入蜀，而散關以東非國家有。

translations.literal: Tan advanced and urged: "The rebellious Hu disorder the norms; the four seas split apart. If you do not take human feeling and plan restoration, even though you wish to follow the sovereign into Shu, east of San Pass will no longer belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Tan stepped forward and urged, "The rebel barbarians have overturned the order of the realm and the empire lies in fragments. Unless you heed the people's will and plan for restoration, even if you follow the emperor into Shu, everything east of San Pass will be lost to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 夫大孝莫若安社稷，殿下當募豪桀，趣河西，收牧馬。

translations.literal: The greatest filial piety is none other than securing the altars of state. Your Highness ought to recruit heroes and gallants, hasten to Hexi, and recover the pasture horses.
