translations.idiomatic: The highest filial duty is to secure the altars of state. Your Highness should recruit bold men, march swiftly to Hexi, and gather the frontier horse herds.

sentences.zh: 今防邊屯士不下十萬，而光弼、子儀全軍在河朔，與謀興復，策之上者。

translations.literal: Now the border-garrison troops number no fewer than one hundred thousand, and Guangbi and Ziye have their full armies in Hebei—for them to join in plotting restoration would be the best stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier garrisons now field no fewer than a hundred thousand men, and Guangbi and Ziye still command full armies in Hebei. To win them to a plan of restoration would be the finest strategy.

sentences.zh: 」廣平王亦贊之，於是議定。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping also endorsed this, and so the decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangping endorsed the plan as well, and the decision was made.

sentences.zh: 太子北過渭，兵仗鹽惡，士氣崩沮，日數十戰。

translations.literal: The crown prince went north across the Wei. Weapons were poor and salt was bad; morale collapsed. There were battles every day.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince marched north beyond the Wei. Arms were shoddy, provisions were foul, and morale crumbled. They fought skirmishes day after day.

sentences.zh: 倓以驍騎數百從，每接戰，常身先，血殷袂，不告也。

translations.literal: Tan followed with several hundred fierce cavalry. Whenever they joined battle he always took the lead. Blood drenched his sleeves, yet he did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Tan rode behind with several hundred elite horsemen. In every engagement he charged at the fore. Blood soaked his sleeves, yet he never mentioned it.

sentences.zh: 太子或過時未食，倓輒涕泗不自勝，三軍皆屬目。

translations.literal: When the crown prince sometimes passed the mealtime without eating, Tan would weep uncontrollably. All three armies fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince sometimes went without a meal, Tan would weep until he could not contain himself. The whole army watched him in admiration.

sentences.zh: 至靈武，太子即帝位，議以倓為天下兵馬元帥，左右固請廣平王。

translations.literal: Reaching Lingwu, the crown prince assumed the imperial throne. They debated making Tan commander-in-chief of all armies under Heaven. Those at left and right firmly requested the Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingwu the crown prince took the throne. The court considered appointing Tan commander-in-chief of all armies under Heaven, but those on the left and right insisted on the Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「廣平既冢嗣，安用元帥？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Guangping is already heir apparent—why use a commander-in-chief?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Guangping is already the heir—why does he need the title of commander-in-chief?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「太子從曰撫軍，守曰監國。

translations.literal: One replied: "When the crown prince follows he is called commander of the army; when he guards he is called overseer of the state.
translations.idiomatic: A minister answered, "When the crown prince accompanies the army he is called commander of the army; when he remains behind he is called overseer of the state.

sentences.zh: 元帥，撫軍也，莫宜於廣平王。

translations.literal: Commander-in-chief is commander of the army—none is more fitting than the Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: The title commander-in-chief means commander of the army—no one is more suitable than the Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，更詔倓典親軍，以李輔國為府司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this. He reissued an edict appointing Tan to command the intimate army, with Li Fuguo as administrative marshal of the mansion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed. He issued a new edict placing Tan in command of the intimate guard and appointing Li Fuguo administrative marshal of his household.

sentences.zh: 時張良娣有寵，與輔國交構，欲以動皇嗣者。

translations.literal: At the time Consort Zhang Liangdi was favored. She allied with Fuguo in intrigues, intending thereby to shake the imperial succession.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Consort Zhang Liangdi held the emperor's favor. She colluded with Fuguo in intrigues aimed at unsettling the imperial succession.

sentences.zh: 倓忠謇，數為帝言之，由是為良娣、輔國所譖，妄曰：「倓恨不總兵，郁郁有異志。

translations.literal: Tan was loyal and forthright and repeatedly reported this to the emperor. For this he was slandered by Liangdi and Fuguo, who falsely said: "Tan resents not holding overall command and is gloomy with a divergent intent.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was loyal and outspoken and repeatedly warned the emperor. Liangdi and Fuguo therefore slandered him, falsely claiming, "Tan resents being denied supreme command and broods with rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 」帝惑偏語，賜倓死，俄悔悟。

translations.literal: The emperor was confused by partial words and ordered Tan to die. Soon he came to regret it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, swayed by one-sided reports, ordered Tan to take his own life. Before long he regretted it.

sentences.zh: 明年，廣平王收二京，使李泌獻捷。

translations.literal: The next year the Prince of Guangping recovered the two capitals and sent Li Mi to present the victory report.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Prince of Guangping recaptured the two capitals and sent Li Mi to announce the victory.

sentences.zh: 泌與帝雅素，從容語倓事，帝改容曰：「倓於艱難時實自有力，為細人間鬩，欲害其兄，我計社稷，割愛而為之所。

translations.literal: Mi was long intimate with the emperor. He spoke at ease of Tan's affair. The emperor changed countenance and said: "Tan in the hard times truly exerted himself with force. Petty men sowed discord, seeking to harm his elder brother. I calculated the altars of state and severed love to do what was needed.
translations.idiomatic: Mi had long been close to the emperor. Speaking casually of Tan's case, he drew a changed expression: "Tan truly fought hard through the crisis. Petty men stirred up strife and tried to destroy his elder brother. I weighed the needs of the state and sacrificed my love to do what had to be done.

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「爾時臣在河西，知其詳。

translations.literal: Mi said: "At that time your subject was in Hexi and knew the details.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said, "At that time I was in Hexi and knew the full story.

sentences.zh: 廣平於兄弟篤睦，至今言建寧，則嗚咽不自己。

translations.literal: Guangping toward his brothers is deeply affectionate. Even now when he speaks of Jianning he chokes with sobs and cannot master himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guangping is deeply devoted to his brothers. Even now, when he speaks of Jianning, he breaks into sobs he cannot control.

sentences.zh: 陛下此言得之讒口耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, this word comes from the mouth of slander.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, those words reached you only through slander.

sentences.zh: 」帝泣下曰：「事已爾，末耐何！

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said: "The matter is already done—nothing more can be borne!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said, "What is done cannot be undone—there is no remedy!

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「陛下嘗聞《黃臺瓜》乎？

translations.literal: Mi said: "Has Your Majesty ever heard of 'Melons under the Yellow Terrace'?
translations.idiomatic: Mi said, "Has your majesty ever heard of 'Melons under the Yellow Terrace'?

sentences.zh: 高宗有八子，天後所生者四人，自為行，而睿宗最幼。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong had eight sons. The four born of the Heavenly Empress formed their own row, and Ruizong was the youngest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong had eight sons. The four born to Empress Wu formed one group by birth order, and Ruizong was the youngest.

sentences.zh: 長曰弘，為太子，仁明孝友，後方圖臨朝，鴆鐐之，而立次子賢。

translations.literal: The eldest was Hong, made crown prince—humane, bright, filial, and friendly. Later the empress was plotting to hold court herself; she poisoned him and installed the second son Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest was Hong, appointed crown prince—a man humane, bright, filial, and brotherly. When the empress was plotting to seize power herself, she poisoned him and installed the second son, Xian.

sentences.zh: 賢日憂惕，每侍上，不敢有言，乃作樂章，使工歌之，欲以感悟上及後。

translations.literal: Xian daily worried and was cautious. Whenever he attended the sovereign he dared not speak. He then composed a musical piece and had artisans sing it, wishing thereby to move the sovereign and the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Xian lived in daily dread. Whenever he attended the emperor he dared not speak plainly. He composed a song and had musicians perform it, hoping to move the emperor and the empress.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：『種瓜黃臺下，瓜熟子離離。

translations.literal: Its words say: 'I plant melons beneath the Yellow Terrace; when ripe the melons hang thick.'
translations.idiomatic: The lyrics run: 'I plant melons beneath the Yellow Terrace; when ripe the melons hang thick.'

sentences.zh: 一摘使瓜好，再摘令瓜稀。

translations.literal: 'One plucking makes the melons good; a second plucking leaves the melons sparse.'
translations.idiomatic: 'One picking leaves good melons on the vine; a second picking thins them out.'

sentences.zh: 三摘尚雲可，四摘抱蔓歸。

translations.literal: 'A third plucking still may be said acceptable; a fourth plucking—clutch the vine and return.'
translations.idiomatic: 'A third picking may still be tolerated; a fourth—and only the bare vine remains.'

sentences.zh: 』而賢終為後所斥，死黔中。

translations.literal: Yet in the end Xian was cast out by the empress and died in Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end Xian was driven out by the empress and died in exile at Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 陛下今一摘矣，慎無再！

translations.literal: Your Majesty has now plucked once. Take care not to pluck again!
translations.idiomatic: Your majesty has plucked once. Take care not to pluck again!

sentences.zh: 」帝愕然曰：「公安得是言？

translations.literal: The emperor started and said: "Sir, how can you speak thus?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started in alarm and said, "Sir, how can you say such a thing?

sentences.zh: 」是時，廣平有大功，亦為後所構，故泌因對及之，廣平遂安。

translations.literal: At that time Guangping had great merit but was also framed by the empress. Therefore Mi used this reply to touch on it, and Guangping was then secure.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guangping had won great merit but was also being framed by the empress. Mi therefore used this exchange to warn the emperor, and Guangping was spared.

sentences.zh: 及即位，追贈倓齊王。

translations.literal: When he assumed the throne he posthumously ennobled Tan as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne he posthumously ennobled Tan as Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年，有詔以倓當艱難時，首定大謀，排眾議，於中興有功，乃進謚承天皇帝，以興信公主季女張為恭順皇后，冥配焉，葬順陵，祔主奉天皇帝廟，同殿異室雲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali there was an edict that Tan, in the hard times, had first settled the great plan, overrode the multitude's debate, and had merit in the restoration—therefore his posthumous title was advanced to Emperor Chengtian. Zhang, third daughter of Princess Xingxin by marriage, was made Empress Gongshun for the spirit marriage. He was buried at Shun Mausoleum and his spirit tablet placed in the temple of Emperor Fengtian, same hall, separate chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dali an edict declared that Tan, during the crisis, had first shaped the grand strategy, overrode dissent, and merited credit in the restoration. His posthumous title was therefore raised to Emperor Chengtian. Zhang, third daughter of Princess Xingxin, was made Empress Gongshun in spirit marriage. He was buried at Shun Mausoleum, with his tablet enshrined in the temple of Emperor Fengtian in the same hall but a separate chamber.

sentences.zh: 初，李泌請加贈倓，代宗曰：「倓性忠孝，而困於讒，追帝之，若何？

translations.literal: Initially Li Mi requested additional posthumous honors for Tan. Daizong said: "Tan by nature was loyal and filial yet was trapped by slander. To posthumously make him emperor—how would that be?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Mi had petitioned to elevate Tan's posthumous honors. Daizong said, "Tan was loyal and filial by nature yet was destroyed by slander. To posthumously proclaim him emperor—would that be fitting?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「開元中，上皇兄弟皆贈太子。

translations.literal: He answered: "In the Kaiyuan reign the Retired Emperor's brothers were all posthumously made crown princes.
translations.idiomatic: Mi answered, "In the Kaiyuan era the Retired Emperor's brothers were all posthumously given the title of crown prince.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「是特祖宗友愛耳，豈若倓有功乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That was merely the ancestral clan's affection among brothers. How can it compare with Tan's meritorious service?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That was only the ancestral clan's brotherly affection. How can it compare with Tan's actual merit?

sentences.zh: 」於是追帝號。

translations.literal: Thereupon they pursued the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the imperial posthumous title was granted.

sentences.zh: 遣使迎喪彭原，既至城門，喪輴不動。

translations.literal: They sent emissaries to escort the coffin from Pengyuan. When it reached the city gate the funeral carriage would not move.
translations.idiomatic: Emissaries were sent to bring the coffin from Pengyuan. When it reached the city gate the funeral carriage would not budge.

sentences.zh: 帝謂泌曰：「豈有恨邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said to Mi: "Could there be resentment?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Mi, "Does he still harbor resentment?

sentences.zh: 卿往祭之，以白朕意。

translations.literal: You go sacrifice to him and explain my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Go offer sacrifice on my behalf and speak my mind to him.

sentences.zh: 且卿及知倓艱難定策者。

translations.literal: Moreover you knew Tan's hardship in settling the strategy.
translations.idiomatic: You, moreover, shared in the hardships of settling the strategy with him.

sentences.zh: 」泌為挽詞二解，追述倓誌，命挽士唱，泌因進輴，乃行，觀者皆為垂泣。

translations.literal: Mi composed two stanzas of elegiac verse recounting Tan's intent, ordered the pallbearers to sing them. Mi then advanced the carriage and it moved. All who watched wept.
translations.idiomatic: Mi composed two stanzas of elegy recounting Tan's purpose and had the bearers sing them. He then pressed the carriage forward and it moved. All who looked on wept.

sentences.zh: 彭王亻堇，始王新城，進封彭。

translations.literal: Prince Peng Jin—initially Prince of Xincheng, advanced to Prince Peng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Peng, Jin, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Xincheng and later advanced to Prince of Peng.

sentences.zh: 史思明陷河、洛，人心震騷，群臣請以諸王臨統方鎮兵，遙相維壓。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming seized He and Luo, hearts shook and trembled. Ministers requested that several princes take command of the regional armies of the circuits in person, distantly linking pressure.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming seized the He and Luo regions, public morale shook. Ministers urged that several princes take personal command of the frontier armies, coordinating pressure from afar.

sentences.zh: 於是詔亻堇充河西節度，兗王北庭，涇王隴右，杞王陜西，興王鳳翔，並為大使。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict appointed Jin as Hexi military commissioner, the Prince of Yan Beiting, the Prince of Jing Longyou, the Prince of Qi Shaanxi, the Prince of Xing Fengxiang—all as grand envoys.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then appointed Jin military commissioner of Hexi, the Prince of Yan of Beiting, the Prince of Jing of Longyou, the Prince of Qi of Shaanxi, and the Prince of Xing of Fengxiang—all as grand commissioners.

sentences.zh: 是歲亻堇薨。

translations.literal: That year Jin died.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Jin died.

sentences.zh: 子鎮為常山郡王。

translations.literal: His son Zhen was Prince of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen was enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 兗王亻閑，始王潁川，進王兗。

translations.literal: Prince Yan Xian—initially Prince of Yingchuan, advanced to Prince Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan, Xian, was first Prince of Yingchuan and later advanced to Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Baoying.

sentences.zh: 涇王侹，始王東陽，進王涇。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Ting—initially Prince of Dongyang, advanced to Prince Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing, Ting, was first Prince of Dongyang and later advanced to Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 興元元年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 鄆王榮，始王靈昌。

translations.literal: Prince Yun Rong—initially Prince of Lingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yun, Rong, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Lingchang.

sentences.zh: 蚤薨，追封。

translations.literal: He died young; enfeoffment was posthumously granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died in infancy; his princely title was granted posthumously.

sentences.zh: 襄王僙，至德二載始王，與杞、召、興、定四王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Xiang Pu—in the second year of Zhide he was first enfeoffed, together with the Princes of Qi, Zhao, Xing, and Ding in the same investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiang, Pu, received his first enfeoffment in the second year of Zhide, together with the Princes of Qi, Zhao, Xing, and Ding in the same ceremony.

sentences.zh: 貞元七年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 子宣為伊吾郡王，寀樂安王。

translations.literal: His sons Xuan was Prince of Yiwu and Cai Prince of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xuan, Prince of Yiwu, and Cai, Prince of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 宣裔孫煴。

translations.literal: Xuan's descendant was Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's descendant was Yun.

sentences.zh: 煴，性謹柔，材無過人者。

translations.literal: Yun was by nature cautious and gentle, his talent not surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was cautious and mild by nature, his abilities unremarkable.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，田令孜逼僖宗幸興元，邠寧節度使硃玫以五千騎追乘輿不及。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi Tian Lingzi forced Emperor Xizong to go to Xingyuan. Binning military commissioner Zhu Mei led five thousand cavalry in pursuit but could not overtake the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangqi, Tian Lingzi forced Emperor Xizong to flee to Xingyuan. Zhu Mei, military commissioner of Binning, pursued with five thousand cavalry but could not catch the imperial train.

sentences.zh: 煴以疾不能從，玫劫之，駐鳳翔，得臺省官百余，乃脅宰相蕭遘等率群臣盟石鼻驛，奉煴為嗣襄王，監軍國事，因還京師，即封拜官屬。

translations.literal: Yun, ill and unable to follow, was seized by Mei. Mei encamped at Fengxiang, gathered more than a hundred officials of the secretariat and censorate, then coerced Chancellor Xiao Dun and others to lead the officials in alliance at Shibizi Post, enthroning Yun as Heir Apparent Xiang and overseeing state and military affairs. They then returned to the capital and at once enfeoffed and appointed the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, too ill to travel, was seized by Mei. Mei halted at Fengxiang, gathered more than a hundred secretariat and censorate officials, and forced Chancellor Xiao Dun and the rest to swear allegiance at Shibizi Post, installing Yun as Heir Apparent Xiang to oversee state and military affairs. They then returned to the capital and immediately enfeoffed and appointed their followers.

sentences.zh: 初，遘執不可，於是罷遘，而玫自為侍中，號令己出。

translations.literal: Initially Dun steadfastly refused. Thereupon he was dismissed and Mei himself became attendant of the left. Orders issued from him alone.
translations.idiomatic: At first Dun refused outright. He was then dismissed, and Mei made himself Left Attendant. From that point orders issued from Mei alone.

sentences.zh: 以裴澈為門下侍郎，鄭昌圖中書侍郎，皆平章事。

translations.literal: Pei Che was made vice director of the Chancellery, Zheng Changtu vice director of the Secretariat—both with the Grand Councilor designation.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Che was appointed vice director of the Chancellery and Zheng Changtu vice director of the Secretariat, both with the designation of Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 遣柳陟等十余人分諭天下嗣襄王所以監國意，皆得進官。

translations.literal: They dispatched Liu Zhi and more than ten others in separate missions to announce throughout the realm why the Heir Apparent Xiang oversaw the state. All gained promotion.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Liu Zhi and more than ten others in separate missions to announce throughout the empire why the Heir Apparent Xiang was overseeing the state. Each envoy received a promotion.

sentences.zh: 玫又脅太子太師裴璩等奉箋勸進，煴五讓乃即位，改元建貞，尊僖宗為太上元皇聖帝。

translations.literal: Mei again coerced Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Pei Cong and others to present a memorial urging accession. Yun declined five times before taking the throne, changed the era name to Jianzhen, and honored Xizong as Supreme Yuanhuang Sacred Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Mei again forced Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Pei Cong and others to submit a memorial urging Yun to ascend the throne. Yun declined five times before accepting, changed the era name to Jianzhen, and honored Xizong as Supreme Yuanhuang Sacred Emperor.

sentences.zh: 河中節度使王重榮率諸籓貢奉，歸者十八九，而蔡州秦宗權自僭號，惟太原李克用不從。

translations.literal: Hezhong military commissioner Wang Chongrong led the various circuits in tribute. Nine or ten of those who returned; only Caizhou's Qin Zongquan proclaimed himself separately and Taiyuan's Li Keyong did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong, military commissioner of Hezhong, led the circuits in paying tribute. Eight or nine tenths of them submitted; only Qin Zongquan of Caizhou declared himself emperor on his own, and Li Keyong of Taiyuan refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 時帝遣使喻重榮、克用，故二人聽命。

translations.literal: At the time the legitimate emperor sent envoys to instruct Chongrong and Keyong, so the two obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The legitimate emperor had meanwhile sent envoys to win over Chongrong and Keyong, and both then submitted.

sentences.zh: 樞密使楊復恭等傳檄三輔，募能斬玫者，以邠寧節度界之。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Commissioner Yang Fugong and others circulated proclamations through the three metropolitan areas, recruiting anyone who could behead Mei, with the Binning circuit domain as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Commissioner Yang Fugong and others issued proclamations across the three metropolitan districts, promising the Binning circuit to anyone who could kill Mei.

sentences.zh: 其偽將王行瑜自鳳州入京師殺玫，而煴與澈、昌圖並官屬奔東渭橋。

translations.literal: Mei's false general Wang Xingyu entered the capital from Fengzhou and killed Mei. Yun, together with Che and Changtu and all officials, fled to the Eastern Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Mei's puppet general Wang Xingyu marched from Fengzhou into the capital and killed Mei. Yun fled with Che, Changtu, and the rest of the officials to the Eastern Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 重榮紿使迎之，煴與官屬別，且泣曰：「朕見重榮，當令備所服迓公等。

translations.literal: Chongrong deceived them with an invitation to welcome him. Yun parted from the officials and, weeping, said: "When I see Chongrong I shall order proper attire prepared to receive you gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong lured them with a promise of welcome. Yun took leave of the officials and wept, saying, "When I see Chongrong I will have proper robes prepared to receive you all.

sentences.zh: 」至蒲，執殺之，因械澈等於獄，誅殺偽官，函煴首至行在所。

translations.literal: Reaching Pu they seized and killed him, chained Che and others in prison, executed the false officials, and sent Yun's head in a box to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: At Pu they seized and killed him, threw Che and the others into chains, executed the puppet officials, and sent Yun's head in a box to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 煴即偽位凡九月敗。

translations.literal: Yun held the false throne altogether nine months before defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's puppet reign lasted nine months before it collapsed.

sentences.zh: 始，煴首至，群臣白帝禦興元南門受之，百官稱賀。

translations.literal: At first when Yun's head arrived the officials told the emperor to receive it at the south gate of Xingyuan. Officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun's head first arrived, officials urged the emperor to receive it at the south gate of Xingyuan. The court offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 太常博士殷盈孫奏言：「禮，公族有罪，有司曰：『某之罪在大辟。

translations.literal: Academician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yin Yingsun submitted: "By ritual, when a clansman of the ducal house is guilty the responsible office says: 'So-and-so's crime warrants execution.'
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yingsun, Academician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, submitted: "By ritual, when a member of the imperial clan is guilty, the responsible office reports, 'So-and-so's offense warrants death.'

sentences.zh: 』君曰：『赦之。

translations.literal: The ruler says: 'Pardon him.'
translations.idiomatic: The ruler replies, 'Pardon him.'

sentences.zh: 』如是者三，走出，致刑焉，君為素服不舉者三日。

translations.literal: Thus three times, then they go out and inflict punishment. The ruler wears unadorned garb and abstains from music for three days.
translations.idiomatic: This is repeated three times; only then do they leave and carry out the sentence. The ruler wears plain garments and refrains from music for three days.

sentences.zh: 今煴皇族，以不能固節，迫脅至此，宜廢為庶人，絕屬籍，葬以庶人禮。

translations.literal: Now Yun is of the imperial clan. Because he could not hold his integrity firm he was compelled to this pass. He should be deposed to commoner status, severed from the genealogy, and buried with commoner's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yun belongs to the imperial clan. Unable to hold firm to his integrity, he was driven to this end. He should be stripped to commoner rank, removed from the genealogy, and buried with commoner's rites.

sentences.zh: 大捷之慶，須硃玫首至乃賀。

translations.literal: For celebrating great victory we must wait until Zhu Mei's head arrives before congratulating.
translations.idiomatic: The celebration of great victory should wait until Zhu Mei's head arrives before congratulations are offered.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 杞王倕，貞元十四年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Chun died in the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, Prince of Qi, died in the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan (798).

sentences.zh: 召王偲，元和元年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Shao Si died in the first year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Si, Prince of Shao, died in the first year of Yuanhe (806).

sentences.zh: 恭懿太子佋，始封興王。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Gongyi Jiao was first enfeoffed Prince of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Gongyi, Jiao, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Xing.

sentences.zh: 上元元年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Shangyuan (760).

sentences.zh: 佋生，後方專愛，帝最憐之。

translations.literal: From birth Jiao was the object of the empress's exclusive favor, and the emperor cherished him above all.
translations.idiomatic: From birth Jiao enjoyed the empress's exclusive favor, and the emperor cherished him above all his sons.

sentences.zh: 後數撼儲嫡，欲以佋嗣，會薨，計塞。

translations.literal: The empress repeatedly challenged the heir designate and wished to make Jiao successor; he happened to die and the plan was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The empress repeatedly pressed against the heir designate, hoping to install Jiao as successor, but he died unexpectedly and the scheme came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 是夕，帝及後夢佋辭決流涕去，帝鯁悵，故冊贈皇太子。

translations.literal: That night the emperor and empress dreamed that Jiao took leave in tears and departed; the emperor was stricken with anguish lodged in his throat, and therefore enfeoffed him posthumously as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor and empress dreamed that Jiao bade them farewell in tears and departed. The emperor was overcome with grief, and therefore posthumously enfeoffed him as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 定王侗，寶應初薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Ding Tong died at the beginning of Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, Prince of Ding, died at the beginning of the Baoying era (762).

sentences.zh: 代宗二十子：睿真皇后生德宗皇帝，崔妃生邈，貞懿皇后生迥；

translations.literal: Daizong had twenty sons: Empress Ruizhen bore Emperor Dezong, Consort Cui bore Miao, and Empress Zhenyi bore Hui;
translations.idiomatic: Daizong had twenty sons: Empress Ruizhen bore Emperor Dezong; Consort Cui bore Miao; and Empress Zhenyi bore Hui;

sentences.zh: 十七王，史亡其母之氏、位。

translations.literal: For the seventeen other princes the histories do not record their mothers' surnames and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: For the other seventeen princes the histories do not record their mothers' surnames or titles.

sentences.zh: 昭靖太子邈，好學，以賢聞。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhaojing Miao loved learning and was known for worthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhaojing, Miao, loved learning and was renowned for his virtue.

sentences.zh: 上元二年始王益昌。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan he was first made Prince of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shangyuan (761) he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，寶應元年進王鄭，與韓王同封。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, in the first year of Baoying he was advanced to Prince of Zheng, enfeoffed together with the Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, in the first year of Baoying (762) he was advanced to Prince of Zheng and enfeoffed on the same day as the Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 淄青牙將李懷玉逐其帥侯希逸，詔邈為平盧淄青節度大使，以懷玉知留後。

translations.literal: The Ziqing garrison officer Li Huaiyu drove out his commander Hou Xiyi; an edict appointed Miao military commissioner of Pinglu and Ziqing, with Huaiyu as acting regent.
translations.idiomatic: The Ziqing garrison officer Li Huaiyu drove out his commander Hou Xiyi. An edict appointed Miao military commissioner of Pinglu and Ziqing, with Huaiyu serving as acting regent.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，代皇太子為天下兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dali he replaced the crown prince as commander-in-chief of all armies under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dali era (766) he replaced the crown prince as commander-in-chief of all armies under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 八年薨，遂罷元帥府。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died, and the marshal's headquarters was thereupon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year (773), and the marshal's headquarters was abolished.

sentences.zh: 均王遐，早薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Jun Xia died young.
translations.idiomatic: Xia, Prince of Jun, died young.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年追封。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed in the eighth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed in the eighth year of Zhenyuan (792).

sentences.zh: 睦王述。

translations.literal: Prince of Mu Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, Prince of Mu.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年，田承嗣不臣，而昭靖夭，無強王，帝乃悉王諸子，領諸鎮軍，威天下。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dali Tian Chengsi was disloyal, and Zhaojing died young, leaving no strong prince; the emperor then enfeoffed all his sons as princes to head the circuit armies and awe the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Dali (775) Tian Chengsi turned rebellious. Zhaojing had died young, leaving no formidable prince among the sons, so the emperor enfeoffed all his sons as princes to head the circuit armies and overawe the realm.

sentences.zh: 於是以述為睦王，領嶺南節度，逾郴王、渭北鄜坊節度，過韓王、汴宋節度，造忻王、昭義節度，皆為大使；

translations.literal: Thereupon Shu was made Prince of Mu and given the Lingnan command; Yu Prince of Chen and the Weibei Fufang command; Guo Prince of Han and the Biansong command; and Zao Prince of Xin and the Zhaoyi command—all as grand commissioners;
translations.idiomatic: Shu was made Prince of Mu and given the Lingnan command; Yu, Prince of Chen, the Weibei Fufang command; Guo, Prince of Han, the Biansong command; and Zao, Prince of Xin, the Zhaoyi command—all as grand commissioners;

sentences.zh: 連為恩王，遘鄜王，暹韶王，遇端王，遹循王，通恭王，逵原王，逸雅王，並開府儀同三司，然不出閤。

translations.literal: Lian was made Prince of En, Gou Prince of Zheng, Xian Prince of Shao, Yu Prince of Duan, Yuan Prince of Xun, Tong Prince of Gong, Kui Prince of Yuan, and Yi Prince of Ya—all granted the Grand Preceptorate of the Palace with equal rank to the Three Excellencies, yet none left the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was made Prince of En; Gou, Prince of Zheng; Xian, Prince of Shao; Yu, Prince of Duan; Yuan, Prince of Xun; Tong, Prince of Gong; Kui, Prince of Yuan; and Yi, Prince of Ya—all granted the Grand Preceptorate of the Palace with rank equal to the Three Excellencies, yet none ever left the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 德宗建中初，周天下訪太后所在，述於諸王最長，故拜奉迎太后使，以工部尚書喬琳副之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong under Dezong the court searched the realm for the empress dowager's whereabouts; Shu was eldest among the princes and was therefore appointed envoy to welcome the empress dowager, with Minister of Works Qiao Lin as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era (780), Dezong searched the empire for his mother's whereabouts. Shu was the eldest among the princes and was appointed envoy to welcome the empress dowager, with Minister of Works Qiao Lin as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 貞元七年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Zhenyuan (791).

sentences.zh: 丹王逾，始王郴，建中四年，與簡王同徙封。

translations.literal: Prince of Dan Yu was first Prince of Chen; in the fourth year of Jianzhong he and the Prince of Jian were transferred to new enfeoffments together.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Prince of Dan, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Chen. In the fourth year of Jianzhong (783) he and the Prince of Jian were reassigned to new titles on the same day.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fifteenth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of Yuanhe (820).

sentences.zh: 恩王連，元和十二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of En Lian died in the twelfth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Lian, Prince of En, died in the twelfth year of Yuanhe (817).

sentences.zh: 韓王迥，始王延慶郡，以母寵，故與鄭王先徙封。

translations.literal: Prince of Han Hui was first enfeoffed in Yanqing commandery; because his mother was favored, he and the Prince of Zheng were moved to new titles ahead of the others.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, Prince of Han, was first enfeoffed in Yanqing commandery. Because his mother was favored, he and the Prince of Zheng were advanced to new titles ahead of the other princes.

sentences.zh: 貞元十二年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the twelfth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year of Zhenyuan (796).

sentences.zh: 簡王遘，始王鄜，徙封簡。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian Gou was first Prince of Zheng and was transferred to Prince of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Gou, Prince of Jian, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng and later reassigned as Prince of Jian.

sentences.zh: 元和四年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Yuanhe (809).

sentences.zh: 益王乃，大歷十四年始王。

translations.literal: Prince of Yi Nai was first enfeoffed in the fourteenth year of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: Nai, Prince of Yi, was first enfeoffed in the fourteenth year of Dali (779).

sentences.zh: 亡薨年。

translations.literal: The year of his death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 隋王迅，興元元年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Sui Xun died in the first year of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, Prince of Sui, died in the first year of Xingyuan (784).

sentences.zh: 荊王選，蚤薨，建中二年追王。

translations.literal: Prince of Jing Xuan died very young and was posthumously enfeoffed in the second year of Jianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, Prince of Jing, died in infancy and was posthumously enfeoffed in the second year of Jianzhong (781).

sentences.zh: 蜀王溯，本名遂，大歷十四年始王，建中二年改今名。

translations.literal: Prince of Shu Su, original name Sui, was first enfeoffed in the fourteenth year of Dali and in the second year of Jianzhong received his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Su, Prince of Shu, whose original name was Sui, was first enfeoffed in the fourteenth year of Dali (779) and received his present name in the second year of Jianzhong (781).

sentences.zh: 忻王造，元和六年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Xin Zao died in the sixth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Zao, Prince of Xin, died in the sixth year of Yuanhe (811).

sentences.zh: 韶王暹，貞元十二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Shao Xian died in the twelfth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, Prince of Shao, died in the twelfth year of Zhenyuan (796).

sentences.zh: 嘉王運，貞元十七年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Jia Yun died in the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, Prince of Jia, died in the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan (801).

sentences.zh: 端王遇，貞元七年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Duan Yu died in the seventh year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Prince of Duan, died in the seventh year of Zhenyuan (791).

sentences.zh: 循王遹，亡薨年。

translations.literal: Prince of Xun Yuan—the year of his death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, Prince of Xun—the year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 恭王通，亡薨年。

translations.literal: Prince of Gong Tong—the year of his death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, Prince of Gong—the year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 原王逵，大和六年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuan Kui died in the sixth year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, Prince of Yuan, died in the sixth year of Dahe (832).

sentences.zh: 雅王逸，貞元十五年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Ya Yi died in the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, Prince of Ya, died in the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan (799).

sentences.zh: 德宗十一子：昭德皇后生順宗皇帝，帝取昭靖太子子誼為第二子，又取順宗子謜為第六子；

translations.literal: Dezong had eleven sons: Empress Zhaode bore Emperor Shunzong; the emperor took Zhaojing Crown Prince's son Yi as his second son, and also took Shunzong's son Yun as his sixth son;
translations.idiomatic: Dezong had eleven sons: Empress Zhaode bore Emperor Shunzong; the emperor adopted Zhaojing Crown Prince's son Yi as his second son, and also adopted Shunzong's son Yun as his sixth son;

sentences.zh: 余八王，史亡其母之氏、位。

translations.literal: For the remaining eight princes the histories do not record their mothers' surnames and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: For the other eight princes the histories do not record their mothers' surnames or titles.

sentences.zh: 舒王誼，初名謨。

translations.literal: Prince of Shu Yi, original name Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, Prince of Shu, was originally named Mo.

sentences.zh: 帝愛其幼，取為子。

translations.literal: The emperor loved him in his youth and took him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved him from childhood and adopted him as his son.

sentences.zh: 大歷十四年始王舒，與通、虔、肅、資四王同封。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Dali he was first made Prince of Shu, enfeoffed together with the four princes Tong, Qian, Su, and Zi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Dali (779) he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Shu, together with the four princes Tong, Qian, Su, and Zi.

sentences.zh: 拜開府儀同三司，詔有司給奉稍，俄以軍興罷。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Palace with rank equal to the Three Excellencies; an edict ordered the responsible offices to grant a stipend, but soon because of military campaigns it was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Palace with rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and an edict ordered the responsible offices to provide him a stipend, but it was soon suspended when war broke out.

sentences.zh: 謨於諸王最長，帝欲試以事，故拜涇原節度大使。

translations.literal: Mo was eldest among the princes; the emperor wished to test him with affairs and therefore appointed him military commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was the eldest among the princes. The emperor wished to test him in office and therefore appointed him military commissioner of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 時尚父郭子儀病篤，帝臨軒遣謨持詔往視。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Mentor Guo Ziyi was gravely ill; the emperor came to the hall and sent Mo with an edict to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Mentor Guo Ziyi lay gravely ill. The emperor came to the hall and sent Mo with an edict to visit him.

sentences.zh: 謨冠遠遊冠，禦絳袍，乘象輅四馬，飛龍士三百，國府官皆袴褶以從。

translations.literal: Mo wore the far-traveling cap and a crimson robe bestowed by the emperor, rode a four-horse elephant carriage, and was followed by three hundred Feilong guards; all officials of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan wore riding dress and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Mo wore the far-traveling cap and an imperial crimson robe, rode a four-horse elephant carriage, and was escorted by three hundred Feilong guards. All officials of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan wore riding dress and followed in his train.

sentences.zh: 子儀手叩頭謝恩。

translations.literal: Ziyi bowed with his hands to his forehead in thanks for the grace.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi bowed with his hands pressed to his forehead in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 謨宣詔已，乃易服勞問還。

translations.literal: After Mo proclaimed the edict he changed garments, offered condolences and inquiries, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After proclaiming the edict, Mo changed garments, offered his condolences, and returned.

sentences.zh: 於是，李希烈反，招討使李勉戰不勝，奔宋州，朝廷大震。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Xilie rebelled; the pacification commissioner Li Mian fought without victory and fled to Songzhou, and the court was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Li Xilie rebelled. The pacification commissioner Li Mian was defeated and fled to Songzhou, throwing the court into alarm.

sentences.zh: 乃拜謨揚州大都督、荊襄江西沔鄂節度使、諸軍行營兵馬都元帥。

translations.literal: Mo was then appointed Grand Protector of Yangzhou, military commissioner of Jing-Xiang, Jiangxi, Mian, and E, and commander-in-chief of all campaign armies.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was then appointed Grand Protector of Yangzhou, military commissioner of Jing-Xiang, Jiangxi, Mian, and E, and commander-in-chief of all campaign armies under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 改名誼。

translations.literal: His name was changed to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His name was changed to Yi.

sentences.zh: 軍中以哥舒翰由元帥敗，而王所封同之，帝乃使徙王普。

translations.literal: In the army they said Geshu Han had been ruined as commander-in-chief, and the prince's enfeoffment bore the same name; the emperor therefore had him transferred to Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: The troops recalled that Geshu Han had been destroyed while serving as commander-in-chief, and the prince's new title sounded the same. The emperor therefore had him reassigned as Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎蕭復為統軍長史，湖南觀察使孔巢父為行軍左司馬，山南東道節度行軍司馬樊澤為右，刑部員外郎劉從一、侍御史韋儹為判官，兵部員外郎高參掌書記，右金吾大將軍渾瑊為中軍虞候，江西節度使嗣曹王臯為前軍兵馬使，鄂嶽團練使李兼副之，山南東道節度使賈耽為中軍兵馬使，荊南節度使張伯儀為後軍兵馬使，左神武軍使王價、左衛將軍高承謙、檢校太子詹事郭曙、檢校右庶子常願為押衙。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Xiao Fu was made chief administrator of the unified army; Hunan observation commissioner Kong Chaofu left campaign marshal; Shannan East circuit campaign marshal Fan Ze right campaign marshal; Vice Director of Punishments Liu Congyi and attendant censor Wei Qian were made adjudicators; Vice Director of War Gao Can kept the records; Right Golden Guards general Hun Jian was central army quartermaster; Jiangxi military commissioner and Heir of the Prince of Cao Li Gao was vanguard army marshal, with E-Yue training commissioner Li Jian as deputy; Shannan East military commissioner Jia Dan central army marshal; Jingnan military commissioner Zhang Boyi rear army marshal; Left Divine Martial Army commander Wang Jia, Left Guard general Gao Chengqian, Chief of the Crown Prince's Household Guo Shu, and Right Assistant of the Heir Apparent Chang Yuan were made commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Xiao Fu was made chief administrator of the unified army; Hunan observation commissioner Kong Chaofu, left campaign marshal; Shannan East circuit campaign marshal Fan Ze, right campaign marshal; Vice Director of Punishments Liu Congyi and attendant censor Wei Qian, adjudicators; Vice Director of War Gao Can, recorder; Right Golden Guards general Hun Jian, central army quartermaster; Jiangxi military commissioner and Heir of the Prince of Cao Li Gao, vanguard army marshal, with E-Yue training commissioner Li Jian as his deputy; Shannan East military commissioner Jia Dan, central army marshal; Jingnan military commissioner Zhang Boyi, rear army marshal; and Left Divine Martial Army commander Wang Jia, Left Guard general Gao Chengqian, Chief of the Crown Prince's Household Guo Shu, and Right Assistant of the Heir Apparent Chang Yuan, commandants of the headquarters guard.

sentences.zh: 未及行，涇原兵反，誼從帝出奉天。

translations.literal: Before he could depart, the Jingyuan troops rebelled and Yi followed the emperor in flight to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could set out, the Jingyuan troops mutinied, and Yi accompanied the emperor in flight to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 硃泚攻城，誼晝夜傳勞諸軍不解帶。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci besieged the city; Yi day and night conveyed encouragement to the armies without unfastening his belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci besieged the city, Yi day and night carried encouragement to the troops without ever unfastening his belt.

sentences.zh: 帝還京師，復故封揚州大都督如故。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital he restored his former enfeoffment as Grand Protector of Yangzhou as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, he restored Yi's former title as Grand Protector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 永貞元年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Yongzhen (805).

sentences.zh: 通王諶，始王，拜開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Prince of Tong Chen was first enfeoffed as prince and appointed Grand Preceptor of the Palace with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, Prince of Tong, was first enfeoffed as a prince and appointed Grand Preceptor of the Palace with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年，領宣武節度大使，以李萬榮為留後，二年徙河東，以李說為留後，皆不出閤。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenyuan he headed the Xuanyi military commission, with Li Wanrong as acting regent; two years later he was transferred to Hedong, with Li Shuo as acting regent—all without leaving the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenyuan (793) he was named military commissioner of Xuanyi, with Li Wanrong as acting regent. Two years later he was transferred to Hedong, with Li Shuo as acting regent. In neither case did he leave the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 虔王諒，以王拜開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Prince of Qian Liang, upon enfeoffment as prince, was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Palace with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, Prince of Qian, upon his enfeoffment was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Palace with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，領蔡州節度大使，以吳少誠為留後；

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan he headed the Caizhou military commission, with Wu Shaocheng as acting regent;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyuan (786) he was named military commissioner of Caizhou, with Wu Shaocheng as acting regent;

sentences.zh: 十年，徙節朔方靈鹽，以李欒為留後；

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to command Shuofang, Ling, and Yan, with Li Luan as acting regent;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (794) he was transferred to command Shuofang, Ling, and Yan, with Li Luan as acting regent;

sentences.zh: 明年，領橫海，又徙徐州，以程懷信、張愔為留後。

translations.literal: The next year he headed Henghai, then was transferred again to Xuzhou, with Cheng Huaixin and Zhang Yin as acting regents.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he headed Henghai, then was transferred to Xuzhou, with Cheng Huaixin and Zhang Yin as acting regents.

sentences.zh: 不出閤。

translations.literal: He did not leave the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He never left the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 肅王詳，資秀異，帝愛之。

translations.literal: Prince of Su Xiang was gifted and outstanding in talent; the emperor loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, Prince of Su, was gifted and remarkable in talent, and the emperor loved him dearly.

sentences.zh: 建中二年薨，甫四歲。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Jianzhong, having just reached four years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Jianzhong (781), at only four years of age.

sentences.zh: 帝欲用浮屠說，塔而不墳，禮儀判官李岧諫非禮，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to follow Buddhist teaching and raise a pagoda rather than a tomb; Ritual Affairs adjudicator Li Kan remonstrated that this was contrary to ritual, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to follow Buddhist custom and raise a pagoda instead of a tomb. Li Kan, adjudicator of Ritual Affairs, remonstrated that this violated proper rites, and the emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 詔贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him Grand Protector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Protector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 文敬太子謜，見愛於帝，命為子。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Jing Weng Yun was beloved by the emperor, who ordered him taken as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jing Weng, Yun, was beloved by the emperor, who adopted him as his son.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，先諸王王邕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he was enfeoffed Prince of Yong ahead of the other princes.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong ahead of the other princes.

sentences.zh: 歷義武、昭義二軍節度大使，以張茂昭、王虔休為留後，不出閤。

translations.literal: He successively headed the Yiwu and Zhaoyi military commissions, with Zhang Maozhao and Wang Qianxiu as acting regents, without leaving the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He successively held the Yiwu and Zhaoyi military commissions, with Zhang Maozhao and Wang Qianxiu as acting regents. He never left the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 十五年薨，年十八，追贈及謚。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died at age eighteen; posthumous enfeoffment and posthumous title were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year (799) at eighteen. Posthumous honors and a posthumous title were granted.

sentences.zh: 葬日，君臣以位而哭通化門外。

translations.literal: On the day of burial, ministers and subjects wept according to rank outside Tonghua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial, ministers and officials wept in order of rank outside Tonghua Gate.

sentences.zh: 陵及廟置令、丞雲。

translations.literal: For the tomb and temple directors and deputy directors were appointed—thus recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Directors and deputy directors were appointed for his tomb and spirit temple.

sentences.zh: 資王謙，亡薨年。

translations.literal: Prince of Zi Qian—the year of his death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, Prince of Zi—the year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 代王諲，始王縉雲郡。

translations.literal: Prince of Dai Yin was first enfeoffed in Jinyun commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, Prince of Dai, was first enfeoffed in Jinyun commandery.

sentences.zh: 蚤薨，建中二年追王。

translations.literal: He died very young and was posthumously enfeoffed in the second year of Jianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in infancy and was posthumously enfeoffed in the second year of Jianzhong (781).

sentences.zh: 昭王誡，貞元二十一年始王。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Jie was first enfeoffed in the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, Prince of Zhao, was first enfeoffed in the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan (805).

sentences.zh: 亡薨年。

translations.literal: The year of his death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 欽王諤，順宗即位，與珍王同封。

translations.literal: Prince of Qin E, when Shunzong took the throne, was enfeoffed on the same day as the Prince of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: E, Prince of Qin, was enfeoffed on the same day as the Prince of Zhen when Shunzong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 亡薨年。

translations.literal: The year of his death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 珍王諴，大和六年薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhen Shen died in the sixth year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, Prince of Zhen, died in the sixth year of Dahe (832).

sentences.zh: 順宗二十七子：莊憲皇后生憲宗皇帝及綰，張昭訓生經，趙昭儀生結，王昭儀生總、約、緄；

translations.literal: Shunzong had twenty-seven sons: Empress Zhuangxian bore Emperor Xianzong and Wan; Zhang Zhaoxun bore Jing; Zhao Zhaoyi bore Jie; Wang Zhaoyi bore Zong, Yue, and Chun;
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong had twenty-seven sons: Empress Zhuangxian bore Emperor Xianzong and Wan; Zhang Zhaoxun bore Jing; Zhao Zhaoyi bore Jie; and Wang Zhaoyi bore Zong, Yue, and Chun;

sentences.zh: 余二十王，史亡母之氏、位，四王蚤薨，亡官謚。

translations.literal: For the remaining twenty princes the histories do not record their mothers' surnames and ranks; four princes died young and their offices and posthumous titles are lost.
translations.idiomatic: For the other twenty princes the histories do not record their mothers' surnames or titles. Four died young, and their offices and posthumous titles are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 均王緯，初名沔。

translations.literal: Prince of Jun Wei, original name Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, Prince of Jun, was originally named Mian.

sentences.zh: 王洋川，後進王。

translations.literal: He was made Prince of Yangchuan and later advanced in princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Yangchuan and later advanced in princely rank.

sentences.zh: 王三十三年，開成二年薨。

translations.literal: He held princely rank for thirty-three years and died in the second year of Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He held princely rank for thirty-three years and died in the second year of Kaicheng (837).

sentences.zh: 漵王縱，初名洵。

translations.literal: Prince of Xu Zong, original name Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Zong, Prince of Xu, was originally named Xun.

sentences.zh: 王臨淮，後進王。

translations.literal: He was made Prince of Linhuai and later advanced in princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Linhuai and later advanced in princely rank.

sentences.zh: 王三十二年，開成元年薨。

translations.literal: He held princely rank for thirty-two years and died in the first year of Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He held princely rank for thirty-two years and died in the first year of Kaicheng (836).

sentences.zh: 莒王紓，初名浼。

translations.literal: Prince of Ju Shu, original name Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, Prince of Ju, was originally named Mei.

sentences.zh: 為秘書監。

translations.literal: He served as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 王弘農，後進王。

translations.literal: He was made Prince of Hongnong and later advanced in princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Hongnong and later advanced in princely rank.

sentences.zh: 王二十九年，大和八年薨。

translations.literal: He held princely rank for twenty-nine years and died in the eighth year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: He held princely rank for twenty-nine years and died in the eighth year of Dahe (834).

sentences.zh: 密王綢，初名訁永。

translations.literal: Prince Mi Chou, original name Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Chou, Prince of Mi, was originally named Yong.

sentences.zh: 王漢東，後進王。

translations.literal: He was made Prince of Handong and later advanced in princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Handong and later advanced in princely rank.

sentences.zh: 王三年，元和二年薨。

translations.literal: He held princely rank for three years and died in the second year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He held princely rank for three years and died in the second year of Yuanhe (807).

sentences.zh: 邵王約，初名漵。

translations.literal: Prince Shao Yue, original name Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, Prince of Shao, was originally named Xu.

sentences.zh: 為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He served as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 王高平，進王。

translations.literal: He was made Prince of Gaoping and advanced in princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoping and later advanced in princely rank.

sentences.zh: 王二年，元和元年薨。

translations.literal: He held princely rank for two years and died in the first year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He held princely rank for two years and died in the first year of Yuanhe (806).

sentences.zh: 集王緗，初名淮。

translations.literal: Prince Ji Xiang, original name Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, Prince of Ji, was originally named Huai.

sentences.zh: 王宣城，進王。

translations.literal: He was made Prince of Xuancheng and advanced in princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng and later advanced in princely rank.

sentences.zh: 王十八年，長慶二年薨。

translations.literal: He held princely rank for eighteen years and died in the second year of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: He held princely rank for eighteen years and died in the second year of Changqing (822).

sentences.zh: 冀王絿，初名湑。

translations.literal: Prince Ji Qiu, original name Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu, Prince of Ji, was originally named Xu.

sentences.zh: 為太常卿。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 王德陽，進王。

translations.literal: He was made Prince of Deyang and advanced in princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Deyang and later advanced in princely rank.

sentences.zh: 王三十年，大和九年薨。

translations.literal: He held princely rank for thirty years and died in the ninth year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: He held princely rank for thirty years and died in the ninth year of Dahe (835).

sentences.zh: 和王綺，初名浥。

translations.literal: Prince He Qi, original name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, Prince of He, was originally named Yi.

sentences.zh: 王河東，進王。

translations.literal: He was made Prince of Hedong and advanced in princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Hedong and later advanced in princely rank.

sentences.zh: 王二十八年，太和七年薨。

translations.literal: He held princely rank for twenty-eight years and died in the seventh year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He held princely rank for twenty-eight years and died in the seventh year of Taihe (833).

sentences.zh: 衡王絢，王二十二年，寶歷二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Heng Xuan held princely rank for twenty-two years and died in the second year of Baoli.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, Prince of Heng, held princely rank for twenty-two years and died in the second year of Baoli (826).

sentences.zh: 會王纁，王六年，元和五年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Hui Xun held princely rank for six years and died in the fifth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, Prince of Hui, held princely rank for six years and died in the fifth year of Yuanhe (810).

sentences.zh: 福王綰，歷魏博節度大使。

translations.literal: Prince Fu Wan had served as military commissioner of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, Prince of Fu, had served as military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 咸通元年，進拜司空。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantong he was advanced and appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiantong (860) he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 王五十七年，咸通二年薨。

translations.literal: He held princely rank for fifty-seven years and died in the second year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: He held princely rank for fifty-seven years and died in the second year of Xiantong (861).

sentences.zh: 珍王繕，初名況。

translations.literal: Prince Zhen Shan, original name Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Shan, Prince of Zhen, was originally named Kuang.

sentences.zh: 王洛交，後進王。

translations.literal: He was made Prince of Luojiao and later advanced in princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Luojiao and later advanced in princely rank.

sentences.zh: 亡薨年。

translations.literal: The year of his death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 撫王纮，咸通初，歷司空，又進司徒、太尉。

translations.literal: Prince Fu Hong—in early Xiantong he served as Minister of Works, then was advanced to Minister of Education and Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, Prince of Fu, in the early Xiantong reign served as Minister of Works and was later promoted to Minister of Education and then Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 王七十三年，乾符三年薨。

translations.literal: He held princely rank for seventy-three years and died in the third year of Qianfu.
translations.idiomatic: He held princely rank for seventy-three years and died in the third year of Qianfu (876).

sentences.zh: 嶽王緄，王二十三年，太和二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Yue Gun held princely rank for twenty-three years and died in the second year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Gun, Prince of Yue, held princely rank for twenty-three years and died in the second year of Taihe (828).

sentences.zh: 袁王紳，王五十六年，咸通元年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan Shen held princely rank for fifty-six years and died in the first year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, Prince of Yuan, held princely rank for fifty-six years and died in the first year of Xiantong (860).

sentences.zh: 桂王綸，王十年，元和九年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Gui Lun held princely rank for ten years and died in the ninth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Lun, Prince of Gui, held princely rank for ten years and died in the ninth year of Yuanhe (814).

sentences.zh: 翼王綽，王五十八年，咸通三年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Yi Chuo held princely rank for fifty-eight years and died in the third year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo, Prince of Yi, held princely rank for fifty-eight years and died in the third year of Xiantong (862).

sentences.zh: 蘄王緝，王六年，咸通八年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Qi Ji held princely rank for six years and died in the eighth year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, Prince of Qi, held princely rank for six years and died in the eighth year of Xiantong (867).

sentences.zh: 欽王績，亡薨年。

translations.literal: Prince Qin Ji—the year of his death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, Prince of Qin—the year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 憲宗二十子：紀美人生寧，懿安皇后生穆宗皇帝，孝明皇后生宣宗皇帝；

translations.literal: Xianzong had twenty sons: Consort Ji bore Ning; Empress Yian bore Emperor Muzong; Empress Xiaoming bore Emperor Xuanzong;
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong had twenty sons: Consort Ji bore Ning; Empress Yian bore Emperor Muzong; Empress Xiaoming bore Emperor Xuanzong;

sentences.zh: 余十七王，皆後宮所生，史逸其母之號、氏。

translations.literal: The remaining seventeen princes were all born of the rear palace; the histories omit their mothers' titles and surnames.
translations.idiomatic: The other seventeen princes were all born to women of the inner palace; the histories do not record their mothers' titles or surnames.

sentences.zh: 惠昭太子寧，貞元二十一年，始王平原，與同安、彭城、高密、文安四王同封。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhao Ning—in the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan he was first made Prince of Pingyuan, enfeoffed together with the four princes of Tong'an, Pengcheng, Gaomi, and Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhao Ning was first enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyuan in the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan (805), together with the Princes of Tong'an, Pengcheng, Gaomi, and Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，進王鄧，與澧、深、洋、絳四王同封。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Ning was advanced to Prince of Deng, enfeoffed together with the four princes of Li, Shen, Yang, and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor acceded, Ning was advanced to Prince of Deng and enfeoffed together with the Princes of Li, Shen, Yang, and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 於是國嗣未立，李絳等建言：「聖人以天下為大器，知一人不可獨化，四海不可無本，故建太子以自副，然後人心定，宗祏安，有國不易之常道。

translations.literal: At this time the heir to the state had not been established. Li Jiang and others submitted advice: "The sage treats all under Heaven as a great vessel, knowing that one man cannot transform it alone and that the four seas cannot be without a root. Therefore he establishes a crown prince as his deputy; only then are hearts settled and the ancestral temple secure—an unchanging constant way of holding a state."
translations.idiomatic: At that time no heir had yet been named. Li Jiang and others urged: "The sage regards the realm as a great vessel, knowing that one man cannot govern it alone and that the empire cannot be without a foundation. He therefore establishes a crown prince as his deputy; only then are minds settled and the ancestral temple secure—an enduring principle of rulership."

sentences.zh: 陛下受命四年，而冢子未建，是開窺覦之端，乖慎重之義，非所以承列聖，示萬世。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty has received the Mandate for four years, yet the heir has not been established. This opens a breach for covetous eyes and departs from the meaning of prudent care—not the way to succeed the successive sages and show the ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty has reigned four years, yet no heir has been appointed. This invites scheming ambition and falls short of prudent statesmanship—not the way to carry forward your august predecessors or set an example for ages to come."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 」以寧為皇太子，更名宙，前以制示絳等。

translations.literal: He made Ning crown prince, renamed him Zhou, and had earlier shown the edict to Jiang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He named Ning crown prince, changed his name to Zhou, and had already shown the edict in advance to Jiang and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復初名。

translations.literal: Before long he restored his original name.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his original name was restored.

sentences.zh: 冊禮用孟夏，雨，不克，改用孟秋，亦雨，冬十月克行禮。

translations.literal: The investiture rite was set for early summer; rain prevented it. It was moved to early autumn; rain again. In the tenth month of winter the rite was finally carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The investiture was scheduled for early summer, but rain forced a postponement; moved to early autumn, it rained again. The ceremony was finally completed in the tenth month of winter.

sentences.zh: 明年薨，年十九。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year, at the age of nineteen.

sentences.zh: 澧王惲，始王同安，後進王。

translations.literal: Prince Li Yun—initially Prince of Tong'an, later advanced in princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, Prince of Li, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Tong'an and later advanced in princely rank.

sentences.zh: 惠昭之喪，吐突承璀議復立儲副，意屬惲，帝自以穆宗為太子。

translations.literal: At the funeral of Prince Zhao, Tufa Chengcui urged re-establishing the heir designate and had his mind set on Yun; the emperor himself made Muzong crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: At Crown Prince Zhao's funeral, the eunuch Tufa Chengcui urged naming a new heir and favored Yun, but the emperor himself installed Muzong as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝崩之夕，承璀死，王被殺，秘不發喪，久之以告，廢朝三日。

translations.literal: On the night the emperor died, Chengcui died and the Prince was killed. The death was kept secret and not announced; only after a long interval was it reported, and court was suspended for three days.
translations.idiomatic: On the night the emperor died, Chengcui was killed and the Prince was put to death. The imperial death was kept secret for a long time before it was announced, and court mourning lasted three days.

sentences.zh: 三子：曰漢，王東陽郡；

translations.literal: Three sons: one named Han, made Prince of Dongyang commandery;
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Han, enfeoffed as Prince of Dongyang;

sentences.zh: 曰源，安陸；

translations.literal: one named Yuan, Anlu;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, of Anlu;

sentences.zh: 曰演，臨安。

translations.literal: one named Yan, Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: and Yan, of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 初，惲名寬，深王察，洋王寰，絳王寮，建王審，元和七年，並改今名。

translations.literal: Initially Yun was named Kuan, the Prince of Shen Cha, the Prince of Yang Huan, the Prince of Jiang Liao, and the Prince of Jian Shen; in the seventh year of Yuanhe all were changed to their present names.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Yun had been named Kuan; the Princes of Shen, Yang, Jiang, and Jian had been named Cha, Huan, Liao, and Shen respectively. In the seventh year of Yuanhe (812) all received their present names.

sentences.zh: 深王悰，始王彭城郡，進王深。

translations.literal: Prince Shen Cong—initially Prince of Pengcheng commandery, advanced to Prince of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, Prince of Shen, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng and later advanced to Prince of Shen.

sentences.zh: 子潭王河內，淑吳興。

translations.literal: His sons: Tan, Prince of Henei; Shu, Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Tan, Prince of Henei, and Shu, Prince of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 洋王忻，始王高密，進王洋。

translations.literal: Prince Yang Xin—initially Prince of Gaomi, advanced to Prince of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, Prince of Yang, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Gaomi and later advanced to Prince of Yang.

sentences.zh: 大和二年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Dahe (828).

sentences.zh: 子沛王潁川郡。

translations.literal: His son Pei was Prince of Yingchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pei was enfeoffed as Prince of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 絳王悟，始王文安，進王。

translations.literal: Prince Jiang Wu—initially Prince of Wen'an, advanced in princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, Prince of Jiang, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Wen'an and later advanced in princely rank.

sentences.zh: 敬宗崩，蘇佐明等矯詔以王領軍國事。

translations.literal: When Jingzong died, Su Zuoming and others forged an edict appointing the Prince to oversee state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong died, Su Zuoming and others forged an edict placing the Prince in charge of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 王守澄等立文宗，王見殺。

translations.literal: Wang Shoucheng and others enthroned Wenzong; the Prince was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng and his faction enthroned Wenzong, and the Prince was put to death.

sentences.zh: 二子：洙王新安，滂高平。

translations.literal: Two sons: Zhu, Prince of Xin'an; Pang, Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Zhu, Prince of Xin'an, and Pang, Prince of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 建王恪，元和元年始封。

translations.literal: Prince Jian Ke was first enfeoffed in the first year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Ke, Prince of Jian, received his first enfeoffment in the first year of Yuanhe (806).

sentences.zh: 時淄青節度使李師古死，其弟師道丐符節，故詔恪為鄆州大都督、平盧軍淄青等州節度大使，以師道為留後，然不出閤。

translations.literal: At that time the Ziqing military commissioner Li Shigu died and his brother Shidao begged for the commissioner's seal and baton. Therefore an edict made Ke Grand Protector of Yanzhou and military commissioner of Pinglu, Ziqing, and related circuits, with Shidao as acting commissioner—yet Ke did not leave the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shigu, military commissioner of Ziqing, died, his brother Shidao sought the commission. An edict therefore named Ke Grand Protector of Yanzhou and military commissioner over Pinglu, Ziqing, and related circuits, with Shidao left as acting commissioner—but Ke never left the palace.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年薨，無嗣。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Changqing, without heirs.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Changqing (821), leaving no heirs.

sentences.zh: 鄜王憬，長慶元年始王，與瓊、沔、婺、茂、淄、衢、澶七王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Fu Jing was first enfeoffed in the first year of Changqing, together with the seven princes of Qiong, Mian, Wu, Mao, Zi, Qu, and Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, Prince of Fu, was first enfeoffed in the first year of Changqing (821), together with the Princes of Qiong, Mian, Wu, Mao, Zi, Qu, and Chan.

sentences.zh: 開成四年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Kaicheng (839).

sentences.zh: 子溥平陽郡王。

translations.literal: His son Pu was Prince of Pingyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pu was enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 瓊王悅，子津河間郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Qiong Yue—his son Jin was Prince of Hejian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, Prince of Qiong, had a son Jin, enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 沔王恂，子瀛晉陵郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Mian Xun—his son Ying was Prince of Jinling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, Prince of Mian, had a son Ying, enfeoffed as Prince of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 婺王懌，子清新平郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Wu Yi—his son Qing was Prince of Xinping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, Prince of Wu, had a son Qing, enfeoffed as Prince of Xinping.

sentences.zh: 茂王愔，子潓武功郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Mao Yin—his son Wei was Prince of Wugong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, Prince of Mao, had a son Wei, enfeoffed as Prince of Wugong.

sentences.zh: 淄王忄辦，開成元年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Zi Xie died in the first year of Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xie, Prince of Zi, died in the first year of Kaicheng (836).

sentences.zh: 子浣許昌郡王，渙馮翊郡王。

translations.literal: His sons: Huan, Prince of Xuchang commandery; Huan, Prince of Fengyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Huan, Prince of Xuchang, and Huan, Prince of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 衢王詹，子涉晉平郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Qu Zhan—his son She was Prince of Jinping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan, Prince of Qu, had a son She, enfeoffed as Prince of Jinping.

sentences.zh: 澶王忄充，子濘雁門郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Chan Chong—his son Ning was Prince of Yanmen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, Prince of Chan, had a son Ning, enfeoffed as Prince of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 棣王惴，大中六年始王，與彭、信二王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Di Zhui was first enfeoffed in the sixth year of Dazhong, together with the two princes of Peng and Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhui, Prince of Di, was first enfeoffed in the sixth year of Dazhong (852), together with the Princes of Peng and Xin.

sentences.zh: 咸通三年薨，無嗣。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Xiantong, without heirs.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Xiantong (862), leaving no heirs.

sentences.zh: 彭王惕，乾寧中，韓建殺之石堤谷。

translations.literal: Prince Peng Ti—in the Qianning era Han Jian killed him at Shidi Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Ti, Prince of Peng, was killed by Han Jian at Shidi Valley during the Qianning era (894–898).

sentences.zh: 無嗣。

translations.literal: No heirs.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heirs.

sentences.zh: 信王憻，咸通八年薨，無嗣。

translations.literal: Prince Xin Tan died in the eighth year of Xiantong, without heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Tan, Prince of Xin, died in the eighth year of Xiantong (867), leaving no heirs.

sentences.zh: 榮王忄責，咸通三年始王。

translations.literal: Prince Rong Cui was first enfeoffed in the third year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui, Prince of Rong, was first enfeoffed in the third year of Xiantong (862).

sentences.zh: 廣明初，拜司空。

translations.literal: In early Guangming he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangming era (880–881) he was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子令平嗣王。

translations.literal: His son Lingping succeeded as heir-prince.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lingping succeeded to the princely title.

sentences.zh: 凡八王，史失其薨年。

translations.literal: In all, eight princes—the histories have lost the years of their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Eight princes in all—the histories do not record the years of their deaths.

sentences.zh: 穆宗五子：恭僖皇后生敬宗皇帝，貞獻皇后生文宗皇帝，宣懿皇后生武宗皇帝；

translations.literal: Muzong had five sons: Empress Gongxi bore Emperor Jingzong; Empress Zhenxian bore Emperor Wenzong; Empress Xuanyi bore Emperor Wuzong;
translations.idiomatic: Muzong had five sons: Empress Gongxi bore Emperor Jingzong; Empress Zhenxian bore Emperor Wenzong; Empress Xuanyi bore Emperor Wuzong;

sentences.zh: 余二王，亡其母之氏、位。

translations.literal: The remaining two princes—their mothers' surnames and ranks are lost.
translations.idiomatic: The other two princes' mothers' surnames and ranks are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 安王溶。

translations.literal: Prince An Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, Prince of An.

sentences.zh: 初，楊賢妃得寵於文宗，晚稍多疾，妃陰請以王為嗣，密為自安地。

translations.literal: Initially Consort Yang Xian won favor with Wenzong. In her later years she grew somewhat ill; the consort secretly asked that the Prince be made heir, quietly securing a place of safety for herself.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang Xian had once been favored by Wenzong. When she grew ill in her later years, she secretly urged that Prince An be named heir, quietly securing her own safety.

sentences.zh: 帝與宰相李玨謀，玨謂不可，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor deliberated with the chief minister Li Jue; Jue said it could not be done, and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted Chief Minister Li Jue, who argued against it, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 乃帝崩，仇士良立武宗，欲重己功，即擿溶嘗欲以為太子事，殺之。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Qiu Shiliang enthroned Wuzong and, wishing to magnify his own achievement, immediately exposed Rong's having once sought to be made crown prince and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, the eunuch Qiu Shiliang enthroned Wuzong and, eager to magnify his own role, immediately exposed Rong's earlier bid for the crown princehood and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 敬宗五子：妃郭氏生普，余四王，亡母之氏、位。

translations.literal: Jingzong had five sons: Consort Guo bore Pu; the remaining four princes—their mothers' surnames and ranks are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong had five sons: Consort Guo bore Pu; for the other four princes, their mothers' surnames and ranks are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 文宗二子：王德妃生永，後宮生宗儉。

translations.literal: Wenzong had two sons: Consort Wang De bore Yong; the rear palace bore Zongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong had two sons: Consort Wang De bore Yong; a woman of the inner palace bore Zongjian.

sentences.zh: 莊恪太子永，大和四年始王魯。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhuangke Yong was first made Prince of Lu in the fourth year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhuangke Yong was first enfeoffed as Prince of Lu in the fourth year of Dahe (830).

sentences.zh: 帝以王幼，宜得賢輔，因召見傅和元亮。

translations.literal: The emperor considered the Prince young and in need of worthy assistants; he therefore summoned and interviewed the tutors He and Yuanliang.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Prince was young and deserved worthy tutors, the emperor summoned and examined He and Yuanliang.

sentences.zh: 元亮以卒史進，有所問，不能答。

translations.literal: Yuanliang had entered service as a clerk; when questioned he could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang had risen from the ranks of clerks; when questioned, he could not answer.

sentences.zh: 帝責謂宰相：「王可教，官屬應任士大夫賢者，寧元亮比邪！
