translations.literal: The emperor rebuked the chief ministers: "The Prince can be taught; his staff should be worthy scholar-officials—is Yuanliang fit for such comparison!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproached his chief ministers: "The Prince can be educated, and his staff should be drawn from worthy scholar-officials—is Yuanliang worthy of such a post?"

sentences.zh: 」於是劇選戶部侍郎庾敬休兼王傅，太常卿鄭肅兼長史，戶部郎中李踐方兼司馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon they strenuously selected Vice Minister of Revenue Yu Jingxiu as concurrent Prince's tutor, Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Su as concurrent chief administrator, and Director of the Revenue Bureau Li Jianfang as concurrent marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Vice Minister of Revenue Yu Jingxiu appointed tutor to the Prince, Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Su chief administrator, and Director of the Revenue Bureau Li Jianfang marshal—all concurrent posts.

sentences.zh: 六年，遂立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (832) he was formally named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝承寶歷荒怠，身勤儉率天下，謂晉王生謹敏，欲引為嗣，會蚤夭，故久不議東宮事。

translations.literal: The emperor, inheriting the negligent excess of the Baoli reign, personally practiced thrift to lead all under Heaven. He considered Prince Jin prudent and quick-witted and wished to make him heir; but Jin died young, and therefore he long delayed deliberating on Eastern Palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Inheriting the dissolute neglect of the Baoli era, the emperor personally practiced thrift to set an example for the realm. He had regarded Prince Jin as prudent and quick-witted and meant to make him heir, but when Jin died young he long put off naming a crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及太子立，天下屬心焉。

translations.literal: Once the crown prince was established, all under Heaven turned their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: Once the crown prince was installed, the hopes of the empire settled upon him.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，詔宮臣詣崇明門謁朔望，侍讀偶日入對。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng, an edict ordered palace officials to proceed to Chongming Gate to pay homage on the new and full moons; the tutors were to enter for audience on alternating days.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaicheng (838), an edict directed palace officials to attend Chongming Gate for the new- and full-moon observances, while the crown prince's tutors were to enter the palace for audience on alternate days.

sentences.zh: 太子稍事燕豫，不能壹循法，保傅戒告， 不納。

translations.literal: The crown prince gradually gave himself to feasting and ease, unable to abide uniformly by the rules; the tutors and guardians admonished him but he would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince gradually turned to feasting and ease and could no longer keep strictly to the rules. His tutors and guardians warned him, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 又母愛弛，楊賢妃方幸，數譖之。

translations.literal: Moreover his mother's love had grown slack; Consort Yang Xian was then in favor and repeatedly slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his mother's affection had cooled, while Consort Yang Xian was then in favor and repeatedly slandered him.

sentences.zh: 帝它日震怒，禦延英，引見群臣，詔曰：「太子多過失，不可屬天下，其議廢之。

translations.literal: Another day the emperor erupted in wrath, took the throne at Yanying, summoned the ministers, and decreed: "The crown prince has many faults and cannot be entrusted with all under Heaven—deliberate on deposing him."
translations.idiomatic: On another day the emperor flew into a rage, held court at Yanying, summoned the ministers, and declared: "The crown prince has committed many faults and cannot be entrusted with the realm. Consider deposing him."

sentences.zh: 」群臣頓首言：「太子春秋盛，雖有過，尚可改。

translations.literal: The ministers prostrated themselves and said: "The crown prince is in the prime of youth; though he has faults, he can still be corrected."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers kowtowed and said: "The crown prince is still young; though he has faults, he can yet be reformed."

sentences.zh: 且天下本，不可輕動，惟陛下幸赦。

translations.literal: Moreover he is the root of the empire and must not be lightly disturbed—we beg Your Majesty to grant mercy."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he is the foundation of the realm and must not be lightly unsettled. We beg Your Majesty to show mercy."

sentences.zh: 」御史中丞狄兼暮流涕固爭，帝未決，罷。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Di Jianmu wept and pressed his argument steadfastly; the emperor remained undecided and adjourned.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Di Jianmu wept as he argued his case without yielding. The emperor could not decide and dismissed court.

sentences.zh: 群臣又連章論救，意稍釋，詔太子還少陽院，以中人護視，誅幸昵數十人，敕侍讀竇宗直、周敬復詣院授經。

translations.literal: The ministers again submitted linked memorials pleading for him; his mind eased somewhat. He decreed that the crown prince return to Shaoyang Courtyard, with eunuchs to guard and watch him; dozens of favored intimates were put to death; and he ordered the tutors Dou Zongzhi and Zhou Jingfu to proceed to the courtyard to teach the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers again submitted memorial after memorial in his defense, and the emperor's anger eased somewhat. He decreed that the crown prince return to Shaoyang Courtyard under eunuch guard, executed dozens of favored intimates, and ordered the tutors Dou Zongzhi and Zhou Jingfu to the courtyard to continue his instruction in the classics.

sentences.zh: 然太子終不能自白其讒，而行己亦不加修也。

translations.literal: Yet the crown prince never could clear himself of the slanders, nor did he further mend his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the crown prince never succeeded in clearing himself of the slanders, nor did he set about reforming his conduct.

sentences.zh: 是年暴薨，帝悔之。

translations.literal: That year he died suddenly; the emperor regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died suddenly, and the emperor came to regret what had been done.

sentences.zh: 明年，下詔以陳王為太子，置酒殿中。

translations.literal: The next year an edict named Prince Chen crown prince and a banquet was set in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict named Prince Chen crown prince, and a banquet was held in the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 有俳兒緣橦，父畏其顛，環走橦下。

translations.literal: A rope-dancing boy climbed the pole; his father, fearing a fall, circled beneath the pole.
translations.idiomatic: A boy acrobat climbed a pole, while his father, fearing a fall, circled anxiously beneath it.

sentences.zh: 帝感動，謂左右曰：「朕有天下，返不能全一兒乎！

translations.literal: Moved, the emperor said to those beside him: "I possess all under Heaven—can I not even protect one child!"
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, the emperor said to those around him: "I hold all under Heaven—can I not even keep one son safe!"

sentences.zh: 」因泣下。

translations.literal: And he wept.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into tears.

sentences.zh: 即取坊工劉楚才等數人付京兆榜殺之，及禁中女倡十人斃永巷，皆短毀太子者。

translations.literal: He immediately had several workshop artisans including Liu Chucai handed to the metropolitan prefect to be beaten to death on the placard, and ten female performers of the inner precincts put to death in Yong Lane—all had spoken ill of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately handed several workshop artisans, including Liu Chucai, to the metropolitan prefect for public beating to death, and had ten female entertainers of the inner palace executed in Yong Lane—all had slandered the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 宰相楊嗣復等不及知，因言：「楚才等罪當誅，京兆殺之，不覆奏，敢以請。

translations.literal: Chief ministers Yang Sifu and others had not been informed in time; they therefore said: "Chucai and the rest deserved execution; the metropolitan prefect killed them without memorializing back—we venture to ask."
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Yang Sifu and the rest had not been informed in time. They therefore said: "Chucai and the others deserved death, but the metropolitan prefect executed them without reporting back—we venture to inquire."

sentences.zh: 」翌日，詔京兆後有決死敕不覆者，亦許如故事以聞。

translations.literal: The next day an edict said that when the metropolitan prefect hereafter carried out death sentences by imperial command without memorializing back, he might also report according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict declared that when the metropolitan prefect hereafter carried out death sentences by direct imperial order without prior memorial, he might still report afterward according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 蔣王宗儉，開成二年始王。

translations.literal: Prince Jiang Zongjian was first enfeoffed in the second year of Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiang Zongjian was first enfeoffed as a prince in the second year of Kaicheng (837).

sentences.zh: 亡薨年。

translations.literal: The year of his death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 武宗五子，其母氏、位皆不傳。

translations.literal: Wuzong had five sons; their mothers' surnames and ranks are all unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong had five sons; for all of them their mothers' surnames and ranks are unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 杞王峻，開成五年始王；

translations.literal: Prince Qi Jun was first enfeoffed in the fifth year of Kaicheng;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi Jun was first enfeoffed in the fifth year of Kaicheng (840);

sentences.zh: 益王峴，會昌二年始王，與兗、德、昌三王同封；

translations.literal: Prince Yi Xian was first enfeoffed in the second year of Huichang, enfeoffed together with the three princes of Yan, De, and Chang;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi Xian was first enfeoffed in the second year of Huichang (842), together with the Princes of Yan, De, and Chang;

sentences.zh: 兗王岐；

translations.literal: Prince Yan Qi;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan Qi;

sentences.zh: 德王嶧；

translations.literal: Prince De Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Prince De Yi;

sentences.zh: 昌王嵯：並逸其薨年。

translations.literal: Prince Chang Cuo: the years of their deaths are all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chang Cuo: for all of them the years of death are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 宣宗十一子：元昭太后生懿宗皇帝，余皆亡其母之氏、位。

translations.literal: Xuanzong had eleven sons: Empress Dowager Yuanzhao bore Emperor Yizong; for the rest their mothers' surnames and ranks are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had eleven sons: Empress Dowager Yuanzhao bore Emperor Yizong; for the remaining sons their mothers' surnames and ranks are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 靖懷太子渼，會昌六年始王雍，與夔、慶二王同封。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Jinghuai Mei was first made Prince of Yong in the sixth year of Huichang, enfeoffed together with the two princes of Kui and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jinghuai Mei was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yong in the sixth year of Huichang (846), together with the Princes of Kui and Qing.

sentences.zh: 大中六年薨，有詔追冊。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Dazhong; an edict posthumously enfeoffed him.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Dazhong (852); an edict posthumously elevated his title.

sentences.zh: 雅王涇，大中元年始王。

translations.literal: Prince Ya Jing was first enfeoffed in the first year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ya Jing was first enfeoffed in the first year of Dazhong (847).

sentences.zh: 亡薨年。

translations.literal: The year of his death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 通王滋，會昌六年始王夔，與慶王沂同封。

translations.literal: Prince Tong Zi was first made Prince of Kui in the sixth year of Huichang, enfeoffed together with Prince Qing Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tong Zi was first enfeoffed as Prince of Kui in the sixth year of Huichang (846), together with Prince Qing Yin.

sentences.zh: 帝初詔鄆王居十六宅，余五王處大明宮內院，以諫議大夫鄭漳、兵部郎中李鄴為侍讀，五日一謁乾符門，為王授經。

translations.literal: At first the emperor decreed that Prince Yun dwell in the Sixteen Mansions while the other five princes resided in the inner court of Daming Palace; Remonstrance Officer Zheng Zhang and Bureau Director of the Military Ministry Li Ye were made tutors; every five days they paid homage at Qianfu Gate and taught the princes the classics.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor decreed that Prince Yun reside in the Sixteen Mansions while the other five princes lived in the inner court of Daming Palace. Remonstrance Officer Zheng Zhang and Director of the Military Ministry Bureau Li Ye were appointed tutors; every five days they attended at Qianfu Gate to instruct the princes in the classics.

sentences.zh: 鄆王立為懿宗，乃罷。

translations.literal: When Prince Yun was established as Yizong, this was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yun was enthroned as Yizong, the arrangement was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 滋徙王。

translations.literal: Zi was transferred to another princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Zi was transferred to a different princedom.

sentences.zh: 昭宗乾寧三年，領侍衛諸軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianning under Zhaozong, he took command of the various armies of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianning (896) under Emperor Zhaozong, he took command of the palace guard armies.

sentences.zh: 是時，誅王行瑜，而李茂貞怨，以兵入覲，詔滋與諸王分統安聖、奉宸、保寧、安化軍衛京師。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Xingyu was executed; Li Maozhen bore a grudge and entered the capital with troops to pay homage. An edict ordered Zi and the other princes to divide command of the Ansheng, Fengchen, Baoning, and Anhua armies to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wang Xingyu was executed, but Li Maozhen, nursing a grievance, marched into the capital with troops under the pretext of an audience. An edict ordered Zi and the other princes to divide command of the Ansheng, Fengchen, Baoning, and Anhua armies to defend the capital.

sentences.zh: 天子將狩太原，韓建道迎之，留次華州。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was about to hunt at Taiyuan; Han Jian went out to meet him on the road and detained him at Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to proceed on a hunting tour to Taiyuan; Han Jian went out to meet him on the road and detained him at Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建畏王等有兵，遣人上急變，告諸王欲殺建，脅帝幸河中。

translations.literal: Jian feared that the princes with troops would kill him; he sent someone to submit an urgent report claiming the princes intended to kill Jian and coerce the emperor to go to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jian feared the armed princes and sent an urgent report alleging that they meant to kill him and force the emperor to go to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 帝驚，召建論之，稱疾不肯入。

translations.literal: The emperor was alarmed and summoned Jian to discuss it; Jian pleaded illness and refused to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alarmed and summoned Jian to discuss the matter, but Jian pleaded illness and refused to come in.

sentences.zh: 敕滋與睦王、濟王、韶王、彭王、韓王、沂王、陳王謁建自解，建留軍中，奏言：「中外異體，臣不可以私見。

translations.literal: He ordered Zi together with Princes Mu, Ji, Shao, Peng, Han, Yin, and Chen to visit Jian and explain themselves; Jian remained with the army and memorialized: "Court and field are separate bodies—I as a subject cannot receive a private audience."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zi, together with Princes Mu, Ji, Shao, Peng, Han, Yin, and Chen, to visit Jian and clear themselves. Jian stayed with his army and memorialized: "Court and camp are separate realms; as a subject I cannot grant a private audience."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「晉八王擅權，卒敗天下。

translations.literal: He also said: "In Jin the Eight Princes monopolized power and in the end ruined the realm."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "In Jin the Eight Princes seized power and in the end ruined the realm."

sentences.zh: 請歸十六宅，悉罷所領兵。

translations.literal: He asked that they return to the Sixteen Mansions and that all the troops they commanded be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that they return to the Sixteen Mansions and that all troops under their command be disbanded.

sentences.zh: 」帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 建以兵環行在，請誅大將李筠。

translations.literal: Jian surrounded the imperial encampment with troops and asked that the great general Li Yun be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jian surrounded the imperial encampment with troops and demanded the execution of the great general Li Yun.

sentences.zh: 帝懼，斬筠以謝。

translations.literal: Fearing, the emperor had Yun beheaded to appease him.
translations.idiomatic: In fear, the emperor had Yun beheaded to appease him.

sentences.zh: 建盡逐衛兵，自是天子孤弱矣。

translations.literal: Jian drove out all the palace guards; from then on the Son of Heaven stood alone and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Jian drove out all the palace guards, and from that time the emperor stood utterly alone and powerless.

sentences.zh: 初，帝使嗣延王戒丕、嗣丹王允往見李克用，二王還，建惡之；

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had sent the collateral Prince Yan Jiepi and the collateral Prince Dan Yun to visit Li Keyong; when the two princes returned, Jian hated them;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had sent the collateral Prince Yan Jiepi and the collateral Prince Dan Yun to visit Li Keyong. When the two princes returned, Jian turned against them;

sentences.zh: 又嗣覃王嘗督軍伐茂貞，於是劾奏：「比歲兵纏近輔，諸王階其禍，使乘輿越在下籓，不得安，臣已請解其兵。

translations.literal: moreover the collateral Prince Tan had once overseen troops in the campaign against Maozhen. He therefore impeached them: "In recent years warfare has entangled the capital region; the princes have shared in the disaster, causing the imperial carriage to dwell below the frontier and know no peace—I have already asked that their troops be relieved."
translations.idiomatic: moreover the collateral Prince Tan had once commanded troops against Maozhen. He therefore impeached them: "In recent years warfare has engulfed the capital region; the princes have shared in the calamity, driving the imperial carriage to linger below the frontier in unrest. I have already asked that their troops be relieved."

sentences.zh: 今延、覃、丹三王尚陰計以危國，請誅之。

translations.literal: Now the three princes Yan, Tan, and Dan still secretly plot to endanger the state—I beg that they be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Now the three princes Yan, Tan, and Dan still secretly plot to endanger the state. I beg that they be put to death."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「渠至是邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Have they come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Have they truly come to this?"

sentences.zh: 」後三日，與劉季述矯詔以兵攻十六宅。

translations.literal: Three days later, together with Liu Jishu, he forged an edict and attacked the Sixteen Mansions with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later, together with Liu Jishu, he forged an edict and attacked the Sixteen Mansions with troops.

sentences.zh: 諸王被發乘垣走，或升屋極號曰：「帝救我！

translations.literal: The princes, hair loose, climbed walls and fled; some mounted rooftops and cried out with all their strength: "Emperor, save me!"
translations.idiomatic: The princes fled with hair unbound, scaling walls; some climbed onto rooftops and cried out with all their strength: "Emperor, save me!"

sentences.zh: 」建乃將十一王並其屬至石堤谷殺之，徐以謀反聞，天下冤之。

translations.literal: Jian then led eleven princes together with their retinues to Shidi Valley and killed them, afterward reporting them as plotting rebellion; all under Heaven deemed it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Jian then led eleven princes and their households to Shidi Valley and killed them, afterward reporting them as plotting rebellion. All under Heaven regarded it as a grievous wrong.

sentences.zh: 濟、韶、彭、韓、沂、陳、延、覃、丹九王，史逸其系胄雲。

translations.literal: For the nine princes Ji, Shao, Peng, Han, Yin, Chen, Yan, Tan, and Dan, the history has lost their genealogies—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: For the nine princes Ji, Shao, Peng, Han, Yin, Chen, Yan, Tan, and Dan, the histories have lost their genealogies—that is all.

sentences.zh: 慶王沂，大中十四年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Qing Yin died in the fourteenth year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qing Yin died in the fourteenth year of Dazhong (860).

sentences.zh: 濮王澤，大中二年始王。

translations.literal: Prince Pu Ze was first enfeoffed in the second year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pu Ze was first enfeoffed in the second year of Dazhong (848).

sentences.zh: 亡薨年。

translations.literal: The year of his death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 鄂王潤，大中五年始王。

translations.literal: Prince E Run was first enfeoffed in the fifth year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince E Run was first enfeoffed in the fifth year of Dazhong (851).

sentences.zh: 乾符三年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Qianfu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Qianfu (876).

sentences.zh: 懷王洽，大中八年與昭、康二王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Huai Qia was enfeoffed in the eighth year of Dazhong together with the two princes Zhao and Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai Qia was enfeoffed in the eighth year of Dazhong (854), together with the Princes Zhao and Kang.

sentences.zh: 亡薨年。

translations.literal: The year of his death is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The year of his death is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 昭王汭，乾符三年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Run died in the third year of Qianfu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao Run died in the third year of Qianfu (876).

sentences.zh: 康王汶，乾符四年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Kang Wen died in the fourth year of Qianfu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang Wen died in the fourth year of Qianfu (877).

sentences.zh: 懿宗八子：惠安皇后生僖宗皇帝，恭憲皇后生昭宗皇帝，余六王亡其母氏、位。

translations.literal: Yizong had eight sons: Empress Huian bore Emperor Xizong; Empress Gongxian bore Emperor Zhaozong; for the remaining six princes their mothers' surnames and ranks are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong had eight sons: Empress Huian bore Emperor Xizong; Empress Gongxian bore Emperor Zhaozong; for the other six princes their mothers' surnames and ranks are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 魏王佾，咸通三年始王，與涼、蜀二王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Wei Ji was first enfeoffed in the third year of Xiantong together with the two princes of Liang and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei Ji was first enfeoffed in the third year of Xiantong (862), together with the Princes of Liang and Shu.

sentences.zh: 涼王侹，乾符六年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Liang Ting died in the sixth year of Qianfu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang Ting died in the sixth year of Qianfu (879).

sentences.zh: 蜀王佶。

translations.literal: Prince Shu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shu Ji.

sentences.zh: 威王偘，咸通六年始王郢，十年徙王。

translations.literal: Prince Wei Kan was first made Prince of Ying in the sixth year of Xiantong; in the tenth year he was transferred to another princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei Kan was first enfeoffed as Prince of Ying in the sixth year of Xiantong (865); in the tenth year (869) he was transferred to another princedom.

sentences.zh: 吉王保，咸通十三年始王，與睦王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Ji Bao was first enfeoffed in the thirteenth year of Xiantong, enfeoffed together with Prince Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji Bao was first enfeoffed in the thirteenth year of Xiantong (872), together with Prince Mu.

sentences.zh: 王於兄弟為最賢。

translations.literal: Among the brothers he was the most worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Among the brothers he was accounted the most worthy.

sentences.zh: 始，僖宗崩，王最長，將立之，楊復恭獨議以昭宗嗣。

translations.literal: At first, when Xizong died, the Prince was eldest and was about to be enthroned; Yang Fugong alone argued that Zhaozong should succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong first died, the Prince was the eldest and was about to be enthroned, but Yang Fugong alone argued that Zhaozong should succeed.

sentences.zh: 乾寧元年，李茂貞等以兵入京師，謀廢帝立王，會李克用以兵逐行瑜，乃止。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianning, Li Maozhen and others entered the capital with troops and plotted to depose the emperor and install the Prince; but when Li Keyong with troops drove off Xingyu, they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianning (894), Li Maozhen and others marched into the capital with troops and plotted to depose the emperor and install the Prince; but when Li Keyong drove off Xingyu with his army, they abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 恭哀太子倚，初封睦王。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Gong'ai Yi was at first enfeoffed as Prince Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Gong'ai Yi was at first enfeoffed as Prince Mu.

sentences.zh: 為劉季述所殺，天復初追贈。

translations.literal: He was killed by Liu Jishu; at the beginning of Tianfu he was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed by Liu Jishu and was posthumously enfeoffed at the beginning of Tianfu (901).

sentences.zh: 僖宗二子，史失其母氏、位。

translations.literal: Xizong had two sons; the history has lost their mothers' surnames and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong had two sons; the histories have lost their mothers' surnames and ranks.

sentences.zh: 建王震，中和元年始王；

translations.literal: Prince Jian Zhen was first enfeoffed in the first year of Zhonghe;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian Zhen was first enfeoffed in the first year of Zhonghe (881);

sentences.zh: 益王陛，光啟三年始王；

translations.literal: Prince Yi Bi was first enfeoffed in the third year of Guangqi;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi Bi was first enfeoffed in the third year of Guangqi (887);

sentences.zh: 並亡薨年。

translations.literal: For both, the years of death are lost.
translations.idiomatic: For both, the years of death are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 昭宗十七子：積善皇后生裕及哀皇帝，余皆失母之氏、位。

translations.literal: Zhaozong had seventeen sons: Empress Jishan bore Yu and the Lamented Emperor; for the rest their mothers' surnames and ranks are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong had seventeen sons: Empress Jishan bore Yu and the Lamented Emperor; for the rest their mothers' surnames and ranks are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 德王裕，大順二年始王。

translations.literal: Prince De Yu was first enfeoffed in the second year of Dashun.
translations.idiomatic: Prince De Yu was first enfeoffed in the second year of Dashun (891).

sentences.zh: 帝幸華州，韓建已奪諸王兵，不自安，乃請王皇子之未王者，既又殺諸王，因請立裕為皇太子，釋言於四方，時乾寧四年也。

translations.literal: When the emperor sojourned at Hua Prefecture, Han Jian had already stripped the princes of their troops; uneasy, he then asked to enfeoff princes among the imperial sons not yet made princes; having also killed the princes, he then asked that Yu be established as crown prince and proclaimed this to the four quarters—it was the fourth year of Qianning.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sojourned at Hua Prefecture, Han Jian had already stripped the princes of their troops. Uneasy in his position, he asked that imperial sons not yet enfeoffed be made princes; after he had also killed the princes, he asked that Yu be established as crown prince and proclaimed this to the four quarters. It was the fourth year of Qianning (897).

sentences.zh: 劉季述等幽帝東內，奉裕即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Liu Jishu and others imprisoned the emperor in the eastern inner palace and enthroned Yu as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jishu and his faction imprisoned the emperor in the eastern inner palace and enthroned Yu as emperor.

sentences.zh: 季述誅，裕匿右軍，或請殺之，帝曰：「太子沖孺，賊強立之，且何罪？

translations.literal: When Jishu was executed, Yu hid in the Right Army; some asked that he be killed. The emperor said: "The crown prince was young and tender; the rebels forced him onto the throne—what crime is his?"
translations.idiomatic: When Jishu was executed, Yu hid in the Right Army. Some urged that he be killed, but the emperor said: "The crown prince was young and innocent; the rebels forced the throne upon him—what crime has he committed?"

sentences.zh: 」詔還少陽院，復為王。

translations.literal: He decreed that Yu return to Shaoyang Courtyard and resume his status as prince.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed that Yu return to Shaoyang Courtyard and resume his rank as prince.

sentences.zh: 硃全忠自鳳翔還，見王春秋盛，標宇軒秀，忌之，密語崔胤曰：「王既竊帝矣，大義滅親，渠可留？

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong returned from Fengxiang, saw that the Prince was in the bloom of youth with imposing bearing and fine presence, and resented him; he said secretly to Cui Yin: "The Prince has already usurped the throne; by great righteousness one extinguishes kin—how can he be kept?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong returned from Fengxiang and, seeing that the Prince was in the prime of life with a commanding bearing and striking presence, grew jealous. He said secretly to Cui Yin: "The Prince has already usurped the throne. By the great principle of righteousness one extinguishes kin—how can he be allowed to remain?"

sentences.zh: 公任宰相，盍啟之？

translations.literal: You hold the post of chief minister—why not bring this forward?"
translations.idiomatic: You hold the post of chief minister—why not raise the matter with the throne?"

sentences.zh: 」胤從容言如全忠意，帝不許。

translations.literal: Yin spoke at ease as Quanzhong wished; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Yin spoke diplomatically along the lines Quanzhong wished, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 它日，以語全忠，全忠曰：「此國大事，臣安敢與？

translations.literal: Another day he spoke of it to Quanzhong; Quanzhong said: "This is a great affair of state—how dare I share in it?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day the emperor spoke of it to Quanzhong. Quanzhong said: "This is a grave affair of state—how would I dare to be party to it?"

sentences.zh: 此必胤賣臣也。

translations.literal: This must be Yin selling me out."
translations.idiomatic: This must be Yin betraying me."

sentences.zh: 」乃免。

translations.literal: The prince was then spared.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was then spared.

sentences.zh: 帝遷洛，它日謂蔣玄暉曰：「德王，朕愛子，全忠奈何欲殺之？

translations.literal: When the emperor moved the capital to Luoyang, another day he said to Jiang Xuanhui: "Prince De is the son I love—how can Quanzhong wish to kill him?"
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor moved the capital to Luoyang, he said another day to Jiang Xuanhui: "Prince De is the son I love—how can Quanzhong wish to kill him?"

sentences.zh: 」言已泣下，自嚙指流血。

translations.literal: As he spoke he wept; he bit his own finger until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: As he spoke he wept, biting his finger until it bled.

sentences.zh: 玄暉即擿語全忠，全忠恚。

translations.literal: Xuanhui immediately repeated these words to Quanzhong; Quanzhong was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui immediately repeated these words to Quanzhong, and Quanzhong was enraged.

sentences.zh: 帝被殺，玄暉置酒邀諸王九曲池，飲酣，皆殺之，投屍水中。

translations.literal: After the emperor was killed, Xuanhui set out wine and invited the princes to Nine-Bend Pool; when they were drunk, he killed them all and cast their bodies into the water.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor was killed, Xuanhui set out wine and invited the princes to Nine-Bend Pool. When they were drunk, he killed them all and cast their bodies into the water.

sentences.zh: 棣王祤，乾寧元年始王，與虔、沂、遂三王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Di Yi was first enfeoffed in the first year of Qianning, enfeoffed together with the three princes Qian, Yin, and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Di Yi was first enfeoffed in the first year of Qianning (894), together with the Princes Qian, Yin, and Sui.

sentences.zh: 虔王禊。

translations.literal: Prince Qian Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qian Xi.

sentences.zh: 沂王禋。

translations.literal: Prince Yin Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yin Yin.

sentences.zh: 遂王祎。

translations.literal: Prince Sui Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sui Yi.

sentences.zh: 景王秘，乾寧四年始王，與祁王同封。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Mi was first enfeoffed in the fourth year of Qianning, enfeoffed together with Prince Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing Mi was first enfeoffed in the fourth year of Qianning (897), together with Prince Qi.

sentences.zh: 祁王祺。

translations.literal: Prince Qi Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi Qi.

sentences.zh: 雅王禛，光化元年始王，與瓊王同封。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ya Zhen was first enfeoffed in the first year of Guanghua, together with the Prince of Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ya, Zhen, was first enfeoffed in the first year of Guanghua, together with the Prince of Qiong.

sentences.zh: 瓊王祥。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qiong Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qiong, Xiang.

sentences.zh: 端王禎，天祐元年始王，與豐、和、登、嘉四王同封。

translations.literal: The Prince of Duan Zhen was first enfeoffed in the first year of Tianyou, together with the four princes Feng, He, Deng, and Jia.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Duan, Zhen, was first enfeoffed in the first year of Tianyou, together with the four princes Feng, He, Deng, and Jia.

sentences.zh: 豐王祁。

translations.literal: The Prince of Feng Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Feng, Qi.

sentences.zh: 和王福。

translations.literal: The Prince of He Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of He, Fu.

sentences.zh: 登王禧。

translations.literal: The Prince of Deng Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Deng, Xi.

sentences.zh: 嘉王祜。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jia You.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jia, You.

sentences.zh: 潁王禔，天祐二年始王，與蔡王祐同封。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ying Ti was first enfeoffed in the second year of Tianyou, together with the Prince of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ying, Ti, was first enfeoffed in the second year of Tianyou, together with the Prince of Cai.

sentences.zh: 蔡王祐。

translations.literal: The Prince of Cai You.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Cai, You.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：唐自中葉，宗室子孫多在京師，幼者或不出閤，雖以國王之，實與匹區夫不異，故無赫赫過惡，亦不能為王室軒輊，運極不還，與唐俱殫。

translations.literal: The commentator says: From the mid-Tang onward, imperial clansmen mostly dwelt in the capital; the young sometimes never left the inner quarters. Though titled as princes of states, in truth they differed little from common townsmen. Hence there were no glaring great crimes, yet neither could they bear up the royal house. When fortune reached its limit it did not return, and they perished together with Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: From the mid-Tang onward, members of the imperial clan mostly lived in the capital, and the young sometimes never left the inner quarters. Though they bore the title of princes, in truth they differed little from ordinary townsmen. Thus there were no glaring great crimes, yet neither could they sustain the royal house. When fortune reached its limit it did not return, and they perished together with the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 然則歷數短長，自有底止。

translations.literal: Thus the length or brevity of a dynasty's allotted span has its own proper limit.
translations.idiomatic: Thus whether a dynasty's allotted span is long or short has its own proper limit.

sentences.zh: 彼漢七國、晉八王，不得其效，愈速禍雲。

translations.literal: Those cases—the seven states of Han and the eight princes of Jin—did not attain such an effect; disaster came all the swifter.
translations.idiomatic: The cases of the seven states of Han and the eight princes of Jin did not achieve such an outcome; disaster came all the sooner.
